*Jāti* means commonality (*sāmañña*); *byatti* means particularity (*visesa*). From "guṇavato," "guṇavassa," or "guṇavantassa"—in the sense of "taṃ naṃmhi," the form "naṃ" is substituted for "taṃ," or [it becomes] "guṇavataṃ."

*Guṇavantānaṃ*: [The forms] of those possessing qualities (*guṇavantānaṃ*). From one possessing qualities (*guṇavatā*), from those possessing qualities (*guṇavantā*), from one possessing qualities (*guṇavantamhā*), from one possessing qualities (*guṇavantasmā*). In one possessing qualities (*guṇavati*), in those possessing qualities (*guṇavante*), in one possessing qualities (*guṇavantamhi*), in one possessing qualities (*guṇavantasmiṃ*), in those possessing qualities (*guṇavantesu*).

By the analysis of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) "and for *nt*, *ṭ* optionally" (*ntassa ca ṭa vā*), when the substitution of *ṭ* is optionally applied to *nt* in the locative plural (*yosu*), *ṭā* occurs for the locative plural (*yossa*);
thus we have examples such as "the sighted ones become blind" (*cakkhumā andhitā honti*) and "the monk from the banks of the Vaggumudā was handsome" (*vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhu vaṇṇavā*). Etc.
In this way: *gaṇavā*, *kulavā*, *phalavā*, *yasavā*, *dhanavā*, *sutavā*, *bhagavā*, *himavā*, *balavā*, *sīlavā*, *paññavā*, and so forth.
153. After *himavat*, before the suffixes *-o* and *-simhi*, the vowel *o* optionally occurs; thus, *himavanto* or *himavā*. The remainder is the same as the preceding.
The term *āyasmanto* appears in the formal ritual formula (*kammavācā*) as a dual form, *āyasmantā*, due to its frequent application there; it also appears as a plural form, *āyasmanto*.

Likewise, [the following terms appear]: sati-mā, dhiti-mā, gati-mā, muti-mā, mati-mā, juti-mā, siri-mā,hiri-mā, thuti-mā, rati-mā, yati-mā, suci-mā, kali-mā, bali-mā, kasi-mā, ruci-mā, buddhi-mā, cakkhu-mā, bandhu-mā, hetu-mā, setu-mā, ketu-mā.
*Rāhumā*, *bhāṇumā*, *khāṇumā*, *vijjumā*, and so forth. [These end in] the vowel *u*. *Vessabhū* is formed by the elision (*silopa*) [of the suffix].
And the distinction lies solely in the absence of the short vowel (*rassa*). By the rule “*ekavacanayosva-ghonaṃ*,” when the short vowel is applied, [the suffix becomes] *lā yonaṃ*.
In the case of *vessabhū*, because it is stated that "the suffix *vo* [is used] for the masculine" (*vo pume*) and "the *ve* and *vo* are elided" (*vevosu lussā*), there is no substitution of *ṭā*.
By the rule "there is elision" (*lopo*), when the *yu* suffix is elided, it becomes *vessabhū*. By the optional shortening (*vā*) of the vowel before *ge*, it becomes *vessabhu* or *vessabhū*;

thus, *bho vessabhu* or *vessabhū*, and *vessabhuno* or *vessabhū*. *Vessabhum*, *vessabhuno* or *vessabhū*, *vessabhunā*, and so forth, are the same as *bhikkhu*. The same applies to *sayambhū*, *parābhibhū*, *abhibhū*, and others.
However, by means of the words *gotrabhū* and *sahabhū*, [the forms] *yonaṃ* [become] either *no* or *vo*: *gotrabhuno*, *gotrabhuvo*, *gotrabhū*;
*sahabhuno*, *sahabhuvo*, *sahabhū*. The remainder is the same as in *vessabhū*. 85.
*Kūto* (from where).

After a word ending in the *kūpa* suffix, the suffix *no* optionally occurs in the masculine. Thus: *sabbaññuno*. Except for the rule "after [a word] ending in *lā*, *vo* occurs in the masculine," *vo* does not occur here;
this is because it is treated separately from *jantu* and other such words by the rule "from *kūta*. When *yo* is elided, the forms are *sabbaññū*. Examples include:
*bho sabbaññu*, *sabbaññū*, *sabbaññuno*, *sabbaññū*, and so forth.
Thus, there are such terms as *maggaññū*, *dhammaññū*, *atthaññū*, *kālaññū*, *rattaññū*, *mattaññū*, *kataññū*,
*kathaññū*, *viññū*, *vidū*, and so forth. Here, because the suffix *-kū* is taken in the three suttas— "vidā kū," "vito ñāto," and "kammā"—
terms ending in the suffix *-rūpa*, such as *vedagū*, are not included.
Ending in the vowel *ū*.
[In the case of] *go*, there is elision (*lopa*) of *si* and *s*. *Go*. 67. For *go*, there is substitution of *gāva* or *gavā* before the suffixes *sa*, *hi*, and *naṃsu*. *Gāvo*, *gavā*.
In all case endings except for the nominative singular (*ga*), the word *go* invariably becomes *gāva* or *gava*.
170. After *ubha-go*, the suffix *ṭo* occurs. Thus: *gāvo* and *gavo*. [Vocative: *bho go*, *gāvo*, *gavo*.
72. In the accusative singular (Aṃ-vacana) of the word *gāvī*, *gossa* becomes optionally *gāvu*. [Examples: *gāvuṃ*, *gāvaṃ*, *gavaṃ*; *gāvo*, *gavo*.
71. Of *nāsā*:

The substitution of *ā* for *nāssa* does not apply [universally] because it is a single phoneme (*ekavaṇṇattā*). While the rule "in the fifth case, for the following" (*pañcamiyaṃ parasse*) is in force, the phrase "for *ādi*" (*ādissā*) specifies that *ā* replaces *nāssa*; there is elision of the following vowel (*paralopa*). Thus: *gāvā*, *gāvena*, *gavā*, *gavena*, *gohi*, *gobhi*. 69. *Gavaṃ sena*:

In the word *gossa*, *gavaṃ* optionally occurs together with *sena*. [Thus: *gavaṃ*, *gāvassa*, *gavassa*. In the *Kaccāyana*, it says: "*gavaṃ ce taramānānaṃ*" (if *gavaṃ* [is used] for those who are hurrying).

In accordance with the Pāḷi, the plural form alone was established for *naṃ*; however, here, because it is seen [in the commentary] as "the gathering of horned cattle (*gavaṃva siṅgino saṅgaṃ*"), the singular form is also used.

70. And for *go*, there is *gunaṃ*: together with the *naṃ*-suffix, the word *go* becomes *gunaṃ* or *gavaṃ*. *Gunaṃ*, *gavaṃ*, *gonaṃ*. *Gāvā*, *gāvamhā*, *gāvasmā*, *gavā*, *gavamhā*, *gavasmā*. *Gāve*, *gāvamhi*, *gāvasmiṃ*, *gave*, *gavamhi*, *gavasmiṃ*.

68. After *sumhi*, [the forms] *sumhi* and *go* become *gāvo* or *gavā*. [The forms] *gāvesu*, *gavesu*, and *gosu* [are also used]. The substitution of *goṇa* for *go* was not made because it is a different word (*saddantara*). For the word *goṇa* is seen in all seven case-endings (*vibhatti*). [The following words take the suffix *sa*:
*usu* (arrow), *bhūmi* (earth), *pasu* (livestock), *raṃsi* (ray), *disā* (direction), *vācā* (speech), *ambu* (water), and *cakkhu* (eye).
In the ten meanings [of the word] *attha*, the word *go* is used; and in the sense of a "juncture" (*lagna*), the word *vajira* is used.
This concludes the section ending in the vowel *o*. Thus ends the masculine gender.
*Kaññā*; elision of *s*.
The vowel *ā* occurring at the end of a noun denoting a female is designated as *gha*. Example: *jantuhetvīghapehi*.

“Vā” means that the elision of *y* (*yolopa*) is optional. *Kaññā*, *kaññāyo*. By the rule “*gha + brahmādite*,” the *e* of *gha* is optionally substituted; thus, *kaññe*, *kaññā*. In the *yo* [locative plural], it is *kaññā*, *kaññāyo*.
By the rule “*gho ssaṃ + ssā yaṃ + tiṃsū*,” there is shortening in the *aṃ* [accusative singular]; thus, *kaññaṃ*, *kaññā*, *kaññāyo*. 45.
By the rule “*gha + pate + kasmiṃ nādīnaṃ ya + yā*,” [the following applies].

After the [nominal stem] ending in *gha* or *pa*, the suffixes *ya* and *yā* occur respectively for the singular forms of feminine nouns (*nādī*). [Examples: *kaññāya*, *kaññābhi*, *kaññāhi*; *kaññāya*, *kaññānaṃ*. 103. After the [nominal stem] ending in *gha* or *pa*, the suffix *yaṃ* or *ya* occurs for the locative singular (*smin*).
[Examples: *kaññāyaṃ*, *kaññāya*. [Note: Regarding the rule "after *gha* or *pa*, for feminine nouns, *ya* and *yā* [occur]," the word "*yaṃ*" [is understood].

And because there is no occurrence of the suffix *mh* in the domain of these [cases], such as the ablative (*apavāda*), due to its being a general rule (*ussagga*), the form "in the ten-thousand-fold element" (*dasasahassimhi dhātumhi*) is established by applying *mh* according to the rule "after *smi*, *hi*, and *smin*" (*smā+hi+sminna*), since the section on the frequentative (*bahula*) applies. [Examples: *kaññāsu*. Likewise:
Faith, intelligence, wisdom, knowledge, thought, counsel, craving, and the lute;
Desire, infatuation, movement, illusion, friendliness, intoxication, training, alms-seeking;
the leg, the neck, the tongue, speech, shadow, hope, the Gaṅgā, a boat;
a verse, an army, a line, a hall, a garland, time, worship, play.
Thirst, feeling, perception, volition, craving, and people;
Deities, crabs, lizards, herons, assemblies, and councils;
Mites, *sephālikā* flowers, Laṅkā, voting sticks, sand, and crests.
Visākhā, visikhā, and sākhā; vācā, vañjhā, jaṭā, and ghaṭā;
jeṭṭhā, soṇḍā, and vitaṇḍā; karuṇā, vanitā, and latā;
kathā, niddā, sudhā, and rādhā; vāsanā, siṃsapā, and papā.
Radiance, boundary, patience, shadow; Kshatriya, pebble, wine;
Swing, balance, stone, play; Crimson, girdle, art;
Mare, lambusa-plant, mouse; Basket, sulasa-plant, direction.
Nāsā, juṇhā, guhā, īhā, lasikā, vasudhā, and so forth.
Regarding the phrase “na + ammādīhi,” when the *ga* of *ammā*, *annā*, and *ambā* becomes an *ekāra* (e), there is optionally a short vowel [before the following vowel]. 62. *Rasso vā*.
In the case of *amma* and its derivatives, the vowel may optionally become short. Thus: *amma*, *ammā*, and so forth. The remainder is like *kaññā*. Likewise: *annā*, *ambā*.

After the words *sabhā* and *parisā*, the suffix *tiṃ* is applied [to form the locative], as in "of the assembly and the gathering" (*sabhāparisāyā*). By the rule beginning with "in place of *gho*" (*ghossa*), the vowel is shortened: *sabhatiṃ* means "in the assembly" (*sabhāyaṃ*) or "of the assembly" (*sabhāya*).
*Parisatiṃ* means "in the gathering" (*parisāyaṃ*) or "of the gathering" (*parisāya*).
Ending in the long vowel ā.
*Mati*, in the locative case (*yomhi*)—1,10. *Pi + tthiyam*.
In a feminine noun (*itthiyaṃ*) that ends in a vowel, the *i*-vowels and *u*-vowels present at the end are designated as *pasañña*.

116. In the case of a *pasañña* *i*-vowel following a *ya*, there is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of that *i*-vowel when followed by the letter *ya*. This is because the term *kvaci* is carried over from the rule "paro kvacī" and is included here. *Ye*.

In other cases, the *kārapubbarūpa* (the single substitute for *a* + *i*) does not occur. [The nominative singular is] *matyō*. Except in cases such as "jantvā" where the *y* is elided, there is lengthening:

*matī*, *matiyo*. [The vocative singular is] *bho mati*, *matī*; [the vocative plural is] *matyo*, *matī*, *matiyo*. [The accusative singular is] *matiṃ*; [the accusative plural is] *matyo*, *matī*, *matiyo*.

[The instrumental singular is] *matiyā*; [the instrumental plural is] *matīhi*, *matībhi*. [The dative singular is] *matyā*, *matiyā*; [the genitive plural is] *matīnaṃ*. [The locative singular is] *smino yaṃ*: *matyaṃ*, *matiyaṃ*; [the locative plural is] *matyā*, *matiyā*; *matīsu*. Thus—
Patti, yutti, vutti, kitti, mutti, titti, khanti, kanti;
santi, tanti, siddhi, suddhi, iddhi, vuddhi, buddhi, bodhi.
Bhūmi, jāti, pīti, suti, nandi, sandhi, soṇi, koṭi.
Diṭṭhi, vuṭṭhi, tuṭṭhi, yaṭṭhi, pāḷi, āḷi, nāḷi, keḷi;
sati, muti, gati, cuti, dhiti, yuvati, vikati;
rati, ruci, rasmi, asani, vasani, osadhi, aṅguli.
*Dhūli*, *dudrabhi*, *doṇi*, *aṭavi*, *chavi*, and so forth. 55.
Regarding the substitution of *ṭo* for *smin* after words beginning with *rati*:
after words beginning with *rati*, *smin* optionally becomes *ṭo*. Thus: *ratto*, *ratyaṃ*, *rattiyaṃ*, *ratyā*, *rattiyā*, *rattīsu*. The remainder is the same as in the case of *mati*.

Ending in *ī*. [In the case of] *dāsī*, there is elision (*silopa*) of the suffix. By the rule beginning with “*ekavacane*,” there is shortening (*rasa*). By the rule “*ye passi vaṇṇassā*,” there is elision of *ī*; thus, *dāsyo*. By the rule beginning with “*jantvā*,” there is elision of *y*; thus, *dāsī* and *dāsīyo*. By the rule “*ge vā*,” there is shortening; thus, *bho dāsi* and *dāsī*, *dāsyo* and *dāsī*, *dāsīyo*. 73. *Yaṃ pito*.
The forms derived from the word *paṃsukūla* are as follows: *paṃsukūlassa*, *paṃsukūlānaṃ*; *paṃsukūle*, *paṃsukūlesu*. Or whatever [forms] there may be. From *dāsī*: *dāsyaṃ*, *dāsiyaṃ*, *dāsiṃ*;
*dāsyo*, *dāsī*, *dāsiyo*; *dāsyā*, *dāsiyā*; *dāsīhi*, *dāsībhi*; *dāsīnaṃ*; *dāsyaṃ*, *dāsiyaṃ*, *dāsiyā*, *dāsiyā*; *dāsīsu*. In the same way:
*mahī*, *vetaraṇī*, *vāpī*, *pāṭalī*, *kadalī*, *ghaṭī*.
A woman, a maiden, a young girl, a female spirit of wine, a Brahmin woman, a female friend;
a female gandhabba, a kinnarī, a nāgī, a goddess, a yakkhinī, a doe;
a female monkey, a sow, a lioness, a goose, a crow, and a hen.
*Iccādayo*.

And here, with the elision of the vowel *ī*, there is the substitution of the preceding form for the double *ñ*; thus: *vetarañño*, *vetaraṇiyo*. [The forms] *vetaraññaṃ*, *vetaraṇiyaṃ*, *vetaraṇiṃ*, *vetarañño*, *vetaraṇiyo*, and so forth.
In the *yos* [case endings]: 167. *Najjā dhayāsvāma*.
The word *nadī* optionally takes the suffix *ām*. In the case of *suññaka-āmā* and so forth, the letters *ñ*, *k*, and *m* are markers (*āgamaliṅga*) [indicating grammatical operations].
Furthermore, because it has *m* as its suffixal marker according to the rule "A letter with *m* as its suffix follows a vowel," it occurs after a final vowel; thus, it follows the letter *ī*.

By the rule "When a vowel follows, *y* replaces *e* and the preceding form of *ya*," *e* becomes *y* and *ya* undergoes the substitution of the prior form, resulting in *najjāyo*. Optionally, in the elision of *pa* and the elision of *ya*, [the forms are derived].
*najjo*, *nadī*, *nadiyo*, and so forth.
[Examples of] words ending in *ī*: *yāgu*, *yāgū*, *yāguyo*. *Bho yāgu*, *yāgū*, *yāguyo*. *Yāguṃ*, *yāgū*, *yāguyo*. *Yāguyā*, *yāgūhi*, *yāgūbhi*.
Yāgu-ya, yāgū-naṃ. Yāgu-yaṃ, yāguyā, yāgūsu. Likewise [the words] *dhātu*, *dhenu*, *kāsu*, *daddu*, *kaṇḍu*, *kacchu*, *rajju*, *kareṇu*, *sassu*, *piyaṅgu*, and so forth.

Herein, the word *dhātu* is seen even in the masculine gender because it is stated in the *Abhidhammāvatāra* as "by the mind-element" (*manodhātunā*); some say that this was stated according to the Sakkaṭa (Sanskrit) system.
*Mātā*, *mātaro*. *Bho māta*, *mātā*, *mātaro*. *Mātaraṃ*, *mātare*, *mātaro*. *Mātarā*; there is no substitution of *y* for it.

In the phrase “ye passā,” there is an elision (*palopa*) due to the analysis of the grammatical connection (*yogavibhāga*). [The form] *matyā* is permitted; [the forms] *aññatra mātuyā*, *mātarehi*, *mātarebhi*, and *mātūhi* [are also used].

When the elision (*salopa*) occurs, [the form] is *mātu*. Because of the presence of the *saññā* [suffix], the [particle] *no* does not occur; thus [the forms] are *matyā* and *mātuyā*. [The forms] *mātarānaṃ*, *mātānaṃ*, and *mātūnaṃ* [are used for the genitive].
In the domain of the sixth case (genitive), the form *mātussa sarati* is also seen. [The locative forms are] *mātari* and *mātāresu* or *mātūsu*. [This applies] with the exception of specific cases.
*Pitusamaṃ* (equal to a father). Likewise for the words *dhītā* and *duhitā*.
[The word] ending in *u*:

when the short vowel is prohibited and elision (*silopa*) is performed, it becomes *jambū*. By the rule beginning with “*jantvā*,” when the suffix *ya* is elided, it becomes *jambu* and *jambuyo*. [By the rule] “*ge vā*”...
Nominative: *rasse bho jambu*, *jambū*, *jambuyo*. Accusative: *jambuṃ*, *jambū*, *jambuyo*. Instrumental: *jambuyā*, *jambūhi* (or *jambūbhi*).
Dative: *jambuyā*, *jambūnaṃ*. Ablative: *jambuyaṃ* (or *jambuyā*), *jambūsu*.
In this same way are declined *vadhū*, *sarabhū*, *sarabū*, *sutanū*, and *camū*.
*Vāmūrū*, *nāganāsurū*, and *samānā* are indeed like *jambuyā*.
This ends with the vowel *ū*.
*Go*, *gāvo*, *gavo*, and so forth, are identical to the masculine gender.
The feminine gender.
The neuter: *si*—111.
*aṃ* [is used] in the neuter.
After a noun ending in short *a*, *si* becomes *am* in the neuter. [Neuter. 112. *Yonaṃ ni*: After a noun ending in short *a*, *yonaṃ* becomes *ni* in the neuter.
Even though there is a rule for the constant substitution of *ni* [for *yonaṃ*], in the alternative case where it is "optionally *ni*," [the forms] *ṭā* and *ṭe* [apply].
...are [the forms]. In the long [vowel], *napuṃsaka* and *napuṃsakāni* are neuter. *Bho napuṃsaka*, *napuṃsaka*, *napuṃsakā*, *napuṃsakāni*.
*Napuṃsakaṃ*, *napuṃsake*, *napuṃsakāni*. *Napuṃsakena*, and so forth, similar to the word *sugata*.
Thus: Merit, evil, fruit, form, means—
The ear, nose, pleasure, pain, and their causes;
giving, virtue, wealth, and the eye of meditative absorption;
the root, the bank, strength, and the auspicious net.
The lotus is his emblem, his face, his limbs, and the water-lily;
it is considered his wealth on the riverbanks, his gold, and his fruit;
the lotus leaf is his cemetery, his forest, and his weapon.
Heart, robe, cloth, *kuli*, faculty;
eye, face, vehicle, food, staircase, drink;
mansion, world, iron, flame, beak, staff, seat.
The knowledge of death by instrument, the object of consciousness,
sovereignty, protection, the city of Tagara, the bank, the umbrella, the hole, and the water— such as these; some [of these].

136. *Na nissaṭā*: the neuter form does not occur after certain [words] such as *ekacca*. For example: *bho ekacca*, *ekaccā*, *ekaccāni*; *ekaccaṃ*, *ekacce*, *ekaccāni*. The remainder is exactly like the neuter.
Thus: *paṭhamaṃ*, *paṭhamāni*, and so forth. *Padaṃ*, *padā*, *padāni*, and so forth, are identical to the neuter; there is no difference in these cases.
106. That [suffix] does not occur after *pada* and so forth, nor does it occur as *padassa*. [It occurs] by means of the word (*padena*) as *padasā*.
105. After *pada* and so forth.

After *pada* and other words, *smino* optionally becomes *si*. Thus: *pade*, *pade*, *padamhi*, *padasmiṃ*, *padesu*. The word *bila* is treated in the same way. From the word *kamma*, *eno* optionally occurs by the rule "after *nā* comes *eno*": thus *kammena*.
By the rule "after masculine nouns ending in *kamma* or *thāma*, etc., *utta*" [is added]: thus *kammunā*, *kammanā*. By this very [rule], *utta* is also applied after *sasmā*;
and when *ussa* is the technical designation (*lasaññā*), *sa* and *smānaṃ* are optionally replaced by *no* and *nā* respectively, as appropriate.
Or because the governing rule (*adhikāra*) is fixed as an alternative. [The forms] *kammuno* and *kammassa*; *kammunā*, *kammā*, *kammamhā*, *kammasmā*;
and "from *kamma*" etc., [showing] the suffixes *smin* or *nim* in the sense of the object (*kammani*, *kamme*, *kammamhi*, *kammasmiṃ*); the rest is the same as the neuter.
Words such as *camma*, *vesma*, and *bhasma* are identical to the masculine, except for the nominative singular (*uttato*).
*Gacchanta*: In the case of *gacchantassa*, there is elision (*silopa*) of the suffix *aṃ*; thus, *gacchaṃ*. Except for the suffix *si*, [the forms] are *daṃ*:
*gacchantaṃ*, *gacchantā*, *gacchantāni*. *Bho gaccha*, *gacchā*, *gacchaṃ*;
*gacchantā*, *gacchantāni*. *Gacchaṃ*, *gacchantaṃ*; *gacchante*, *gacchantāni*. *Gacchatā*, *gacchantena*, and so forth, are the same as the masculine gender. Thus.
Yajanta, vajanta, and so forth. [The suffix] -a ending in a vowel (akāranta). [Examples: aṭṭhi;
[here] there is elision of the suffix (silopa).

113. *Jhal* is optionally substituted for *jhal* that follows *y* in the neuter. *Atthīni*. When there is elision (*lopa*) by the rule "elision" (*lopo*), the vowel becomes long: *aṭṭhī*. O bone: *bho aṭṭhi*, *aṭṭhī*; [nominative plural] *aṭṭhīni*, *aṭṭhī*.
[Accusative singular] *aṭṭhiṃ*, [accusative plural] *aṭṭhīni*, *aṭṭhī*. [Instrumental singular] *aṭṭhinā*, etc., which is the same as the word *muni*. Thus...
*Pacchi*, *akkhi*, *dadhi*, *satthi*, *vāri*, *acci*, etc. [These are] ending in the vowel *i*.

[In the case of] *daṇḍi*, because it is neuter, by the rule "in the singular" (*ekavacane*) and so forth, there is shortening (*rassa*), and the elision of *si*. [Thus: *daṇḍīni*, *daṇḍī*. By the rule "optionally before the locative suffix *ge*" (*ge vā*), there is shortening.
*bho daṇḍi*, *daṇḍī*, *daṇḍīni*, *daṇḍī*. "Naṃ jhīto" means *naṃ*. *Daṇḍinaṃ*, *daṇḍiṃ*, *daṇḍīni*, *daṇḍī*. The remainder is the same as *daṇḍī* in the masculine.
Thus are *sukhakārī*, *sīghayāyī*, and so forth. This concludes the section on words ending in *ī*.

*Cakkhu*, *cakkhūni*, *cakkhū*. The rest is the same as for *aṭṭhi*. Likewise for *āyu*, *vasu*, *dhanu*, *dāru*, *tipu*, *madhu*, *siṅgu*, *hiṅgu*, *vatthu*, *jatu*, *ambu*, *assu*, etc. From the word *āyu*, there is no difference [in form] due to the burning of anger (*kodhādittā*).
[Words] ending in *-u*:
*gotrabhu* (in the singular, elision of the final syllable); *gotrabhūni*, *gotrabhū*. *Bho gotrabhu*, *gotrabhū*, *gotrabhūni*, *gotrabhū*.
*Gotrabhū*, *gotrabhūni*, *gotrabhū*—and so forth—in the masculine gender, it is similar to *vessabhū*. Likewise for *sayambhū*, *abhibhū*, *dhammaññū*, and others.
This concludes the section on words ending in *-ū*. Now, *visada*, *visadākāra*, *vohāra*, and *ubhayamuttaka*;
The gender-sign (*liṅga*) is defined as that which serves as the cause for the cognition of "male" and so forth.
One possessing breasts and hair is a woman; one possessing a beard is a man.
That which lies between these two is neuter (*itara*); anything other than both is beyond [these categories].
In those cases where the world uses "he," "she," or "it" in the sense of established convention,
[the terms] "feminine," "masculine," and "neuter" apply.
These are called neuter nouns.
Now, the method for the declension of *sabba* and other pronouns is demonstrated.

*Sabba*, *katara*, *katama*, *ubhaya*, *itara*, *añña*, *aññatara*, *aññatama*; *pubba*, *para*, *apara*, *dakkhiṇa*, *uttara*, *adhara*—these are established as pronouns (*asaññā*) when used in the sense of defining or distinguishing.
According to the rule: “The examples of deficient, redundant, and superfluous words are elided,” one should apply this to the list beginning with *sabba*.
*Ya*, *tya*, *ta*, *eta*, *ima*, *amu*, *kiṃ*, *eka*, *tumha*, *amha*—these are the *sabbādi* (all-inclusive) pronouns.
In the *Kaccāyana*, even though the word *tya* has not been explicitly shown:
"Play is directed toward them, delight is established in them;
seeds grow in them, namely, that beings are born therein."
Because they appear in the Pāḷi, they are included here.

In this context, the word *sabba* (all) has the sense of "without remainder. The words *katara* and *katama* have the sense of "inquiry. The word *ubhaya* (both) denotes a collection consisting of two parts.
The word *itara* denotes the counterpart of what has been mentioned. The word *añña* (other) denotes something additional or subsequent. The words *aññatara* and *aññatama*...

The term *aniyama* means "indefinite. Words such as *pubba* ("eastern") and so forth are terms for the determination of directions and the like. The word *ya* has the sense of indefiniteness. The words *tya* and *ta* are terms used for what is out of sight (*parammukha*).
The words *eta*, *ima*, *amu*, and *kiṃ* are terms expressing proximity, extreme proximity, distance, and inquiry, respectively. The word *eka* denotes number and so forth.
The words *tumha* and *amha* are terms used to designate others and oneself (*para* and *atta*).
*Sabbo, sissa o*: 138.

After *sabba* and the other [words] ending in *a*, *yonaṃ* always becomes *eṭa*. *Sabbe*. *Bho sabba*, *sabbā*, *sabbe*. *Sabbaṃ*, *sabbe*. *Sabbena*, *sabbehi*, *sabbebhi*. Likewise in the instrumental case. *Sabbassa*.
99. *Sabbādīnaṃ naṃmhi ca*:

For the words beginning with *sabba*, when followed by the suffix *naṃ*, there is the substitution of *e* in place of the final vowel *a*; this also applies when followed by *su* and *hisu*. Here, the word "beginning" (*ādi*) refers to a part [of a group], for it is said:
"In the sense of a limit, in the sense of a mode, as well as in the sense of proximity and in the sense of a part."
"In these four cases, the wise man should explain the word *ādi*.

100. Regarding the forms *saṃ* and *sānaṃ*: after the word *sabba*, the forms *saṃ* and *sānaṃ* occur for the neuter [nominative and accusative plural]. *Sabbesaṃ*, *sabbesānaṃ*. *Sabbā*, *sabbamhā*, *sabbasmā*. *Sabbe*, *sabbamhi*, *sabbasmiṃ*, *sabbesu*.
In the word *itthī*, by the application of the suffix *-matvā* (the feminine suffix), that [suffix] is designated as *gha*. The rest is the same as *kaññā*.

*Sabbā*, *sabbā*, *sabbāyo*. *Bho sabbe*, *sabbā*, *sabbāyo*. By the rule "When *gho* [is followed by] *ssaṃ*, *ssā*, *ssāyaṃ*, or *tiṃ*, there is elision (*rasso*)," [we have] *sabbaṃ*, *sabbā*, *sabbāyo*.
*Sabbāya*, *sabbāhi*, *sabbābhi*.
101. *Gha* becomes *ssa* or *ssā* after the *gha*-case endings of the *sabba*-class nouns.

Because the form *amussa* is already established by the substitution of *ssā* according to the rule "after *te*, *ti*, *mā*, and *mū*, [the genitive] becomes *ssā*," the inclusion of the term *vā* (or) is for the sake of subsequent rules.
In the short vowel (*rasse*), [the forms are]: *sabbassa*, *sabbāya*; *sabbāsaṃ*, *sabbāsānaṃ*. In the fifth case (ablative), [the forms are]: *sabbāya*.
102. *Smino ssaṃ*:
After *sabba* and the others, *smino* optionally becomes *ssaṃ*. [Thus: *sabbassaṃ*, *sabbāyaṃ*, *sabbāya*, *sabbāsu*.
In the neuter, it is *sabbaṃ*. According to the rule "for *yo*, *nī*"—in the neuter, for *yo*, *ni* is substituted in the locative (*nimhi*).
137. After *sabba* and the other [words of that group], the suffix *-nissa* does not occur for another [word]. All [forms] are long in the vocative: *bho sabba*, *sabbā*, *sabbāni*.

[The nominative forms are: *sabbaṃ*, *sabbe*, *sabbāni*. In the neuter, they are like the masculine. The words *katara*, *katama*, and *ubhaya* are identical to *sabba* in all three genders. The same applies to the words *itara* and *añña*. There is a distinction in the case endings *-ssā*, *-ssaṃ*, and *-su*.

52. *Ssaṃ*, *ssā*, *ssāyo*, *itara*, *eka*, *añña*, *iti*, *māna*—in the case of *samādīsu*, *itara*, *eka*, *añña*, *eta*, and *ima*, the substitution of *i* occurs invariably. [Examples: *itarissā*, *itarāya*; *aññissā*, *aññāya*; *aññāsaṃ*, *aññāsānaṃ*. *Aññissaṃ*, *aññāyaṃ*, *aññāya*. *Aññatara* and *aññatama* are identical in all genders. The preceding [rule applies].

143. By means of these six [words] beginning with *pubba*, the suffix *eṭ* optionally occurs when they refer to their own objects; thus for the masculine (*yossa*), there is *eṭ*: *pubbe*, *pubbā*. [The forms are: *bho pubba*, *pubbā*; *pubbe*, *pubbā*. [The accusative is: *pubbaṃ*, *pubbe*. [The instrumental is: *pubbena*. The remainder is the same for all genders. Thus are the five beginning with *para*. 139.
And that which is not another is called the primary (appadhāna).
When [words] such as *sabba* function as names (*nāmabhūta*) and are subordinate (*appadhāna*), the grammatical operations (*kāriya*) pertaining to *sabba*-type words do not take place.

The meaning is: "those are all," "those are all-nouns" (*sabbā, sabbanāmā te*). [Examples include: "those dear-all-ones" (*piyasabbā*), "those exceeding-all-ones" (*atisabbā*). Furthermore, when they function as names and refer to something other than their own primary referent (*aññapadatthādo*), or in cases where they are subordinate, the application of *sabba*-type operations is prohibited;
thus, in examples such as "they stand at the supreme-all-ones" (*paramasabbe tiṭṭhanti*), the suffixes beginning with *-eṭa* arise from the end of the primary word.
[This occurs] because, in a descriptive compound (*visesana-samāsa*), the meaning of the final member is predominant. 140. Regarding the connection with the sense of the third case:

when there is a connection with the sense of the third case, the grammatical operation pertaining to the *sabbādi* group does not take place. For example: *māsena pubbā* (prior by a month), *māsapubbā*, and so forth.
141. Regarding the compound with the fourth case (catutthī-samāsa):

in the context of a compound with the fourth case, the grammatical operations pertaining to the *sabbādi* group do not take place. Examples include *dakkhiṇuttarapubbānaṃ*, and so forth. 142. *Ve + ṭa* [The suffix *ṭa* is applied after the word *ve*].

Thus, in the case of *catu* (four), the grammatical operations (*kāriya*) beginning with *sabba* do not apply; since there is a constant possibility of the substitution of *eṭ*, this [rule regarding *catu*] is an optional provision for that which has already been reached.

*Pubbuttara* (eastern-northern) becomes *pubbuttarā*. The remainder is the same as *sugata*. *Yo*, *ye*; *yā*, *yāyo*; *yaṃ*, *yāni*, and so forth, are the same as *sabba*. No form for the vocative of *yādī* (the *ya*-series) is possible. *Tya si*—
128. *Tya-te-tānaṃ tassa so*:
for the forms *tya*, *te*, and *tānaṃ* [in the nominative], *so* occurs in place of *tassa*. *Syo*, *tye*; *syā*, *tyā*, *tyāyo*; *tyaṃ*, *tyāni*—and so forth, all are identical. *So*.
131. Therefore, for us, the form *tassa* occurs for all cases, and for us, [the forms] *tassa*, *no*, or *vā* occur for all case-endings (*vibhatti*).

Furthermore, regarding the rule "tyā-te-tānaṃ tassā," here the inclusion of the letter *t* in *tyā* and so forth means that [the suffixes] *syā*, *sā*, *esā*, and *nāyo* are identical in all respects when applied to the feminine. *Ne*, *te*. *Naṃ*, *taṃ*; *ne*, *te*.
Nena, tena; nehi, nebhi; tehi, tebhi. 132. Regarding *ṭa*, *sasmā*, *smiṃ*, *ssā*, *yassaṃ*, *ssā*, *saṃ*, *mhā*, *mhi*, and *svi*:
even when it is stated as "*ṭa sa smā smi naṃ smi massa cā*," [the rule applies] when the substitutes for those case-endings—namely *ssā* and so forth—follow.

Although the substitution of *ṭ* is established by the rule “that which is substituted for something becomes like that [original]” (*tadādesā tadiva bhavanti*), the mention of *ssādi* (beginning with *ss*) is for the purpose of excluding it when other substitutions such as *yādi* follow.
When *ssādi* follows, the *ṭ* optionally occurs in place of the *m* of *amha* and the *t* of *ta-sadda*. There is elision of the preceding *s* and *r*.
The same applies hereafter. [Examples: *assa*, *nassa*, *tassa*; *nesaṃ*, *nesānaṃ*, *tesaṃ*, *tesānaṃ*; *amhā*, *asmā*, *namhā*, *nasmā*, *tamhā*, *tasmā*; *amhi*.
In the masculine: *asmiṃ*, *namhi*, *nasmiṃ*, *tamhi*, *tasmiṃ*; *nesu*, *tesu*. In the feminine:
*sā*, *nā*, *nāyo*, *tā*, *tāyo*. The accusative: *naṃ*, *taṃ*, *nā*, *nāyo*, *tā*, *tāyo*.
The dative: *nāmhi*—46. *ssā*, *vā*, *te*, *ti*, *mā*, *mūhi*.

Since the term *gha* is used as a conventional designation for vowels (*antassarānaṃ*)—and by that designation, the sounds associated with them are also understood, as in the expression “insert the spears” (*kunte pavesaya*)—it is stated: “after those that have the designation *gha*: *ta*, *eta*, *ima*, and *amū*.

*tassa* or *vā*, *i*, *ho*. *Tissā*, *tassā*, *tāya*, *nāhi*, *nābhi*, *tāhi*, *tābhi*. *Sassa* or *ssāmhi*, *assā*, *nassā*, *tissā*, *tassā*.

According to the grammatical rule that "the words *yaṃ* and *taṃ* are always connected," the word *taṃ* specifies the indefinite meaning provided by the word *yaṃ*.

Because it has been stated: "The word *taṃ* (that) is always appropriate when [referring to] a well-known experienced object, as well as when the object has departed, provided it does not depend on the word *yaṃ* (which/who)," in this very instance the word *taṃ* does not depend on the word *yaṃ*. The examples for these follow their respective order: [as follows].
(1) “Namo tassā,” and (2) “Aggimpi pakkhinā... pe... ñātakārī hi so jino,” and (3) referring back to the word *muni* mentioned in the preceding verse, “savāsane kilese so.
These forms—*eso*, *ete*; *esā*, *etā*, *etāyo*; *etaṃ*, *etāni*, etc.—differ only in the absence of the substitution of *ta* for *na*.
[The form] *ima si*.

In place of *ima* when it is not feminine, *ṭe* optionally occurs before *su*, *naṃ*, and *him*. [Note: "When a noun is mentioned, that which is distinguished by gender is also included."

In the rule *ñāyā anitthiyaṃ*, the term "not feminine" (*anitthiyaṃ*) serves to exclude the feminine gender. Consequently, this also includes the inclusion of the word *ima* when it is qualified by gender within the scope of the application of the term *nāmaggahaṇa*.
The result of this is the establishment of grammatical operations across all three genders in instances such as *tato tassa no sabbāsu*.

Thus: *ehi*, *ebhi*, *imehi*, *imebhi*. Furthermore, according to the rule *ṭa sasmāsmiṃ*, etc., there is either the substitution of *ṭa* for the entire *ima* or for the *ma* of *ima*. Thus: *assa*, *imassa*.
Masculine: *vā*, *te*, *esaṃ*, *esānaṃ*. *Amhā*, *asmā*, *imamhā*, *imasmā*. *Amhi*, *asmiṃ*, *imamhi*, *imasmiṃ*; *esu*, *imesu*. Feminine: *ayaṃ*, *imā*, *imāyo*. *Imaṃ*, *imā*, *imāyo*.
[In the feminine, by the rule] "‘ssā’, ‘vā’, ‘te’, ‘ti’, ‘mā’, ‘mūhī’," there is the substitution of *ssā* or *vā*;
and when the substitution of *tā* has been made, and by the rule beginning with "‘ssa’," the substitution of *i* is made: *assā*, *imissā*, *imāya*; *imāhi*, *imābhi*. *Assā*, *imissā*.
[The forms] *assā* and *imissā* [are derived from] *imāya*. When the substitution (*samādese*) of the word *naṃ* occurs, there is optionally the substitution of *ṭā* for *ima*;
then, having applied the rule "sunamhi sū" and made the vowel long, one obtains *āsaṃ*, except for the forms *imāsaṃ* and *imāsānaṃ*. In the locative case:
*assaṃ*, *imissaṃ*, *assā*, *imissā*, *imāyaṃ*, *imāya*, and *imāsu*.
In the neuter: 201.

In these [cases], *idaṃ* or *imaṃ* becomes *imassa* or *imāni* along with those [suffixes] in the neuter. *Idaṃ*, *imaṃ*; *ime*, *imāni*. *Idaṃ*, *imaṃ*; *ime*, *imāni*. *Anena*, *iminā*, and so forth, are the same as the masculine.
197. *Ime* and *ena* are the substitutes for the second case in the context of direct and indirect address (*anvādesa*).
In the context of speaking about or referring back to what has already been mentioned, *me* and *na* are the substitutes for the second case of the words *ima* and *eta*.
"Exhort this monk regarding the Vinaya, and also exhort him regarding the Dhamma. "Exhort these monks regarding the Vinaya, and also exhort them regarding the Dhamma."
In this same way, it should be applied to him as well.
"You were that one, 129. [the name] of such-and-such."
For a non-neuter [stem], the *m* of *am* becomes *s* before the nominative singular suffix *si*. Thus: *asu*, *yo*. 86. *Lopo musmā*:

This is a restrictive rule (*niyama-sutta*); after the word *amu*, there is always elision (*lopa*) of the [suffixes] *ya* and *na* in the masculine gender. Thus: *dīgho amū*. Although the elision of *ya* and *na* after a consonant (*jhal*) is already established by the rule "elision" (*lopo*), this present rule is commenced as an exception (*vopavāda*) to that.
*Ārambho*, *vacanaṃ*, *patti*, *lakkhaṇaṃ*, *yogalakkhaṇaṃ*, *vākyaṃ*, *satthañca*—these and others are the designators of the suttas.
*Amuṃ*, *amū*. *Amunā*, *amūhi*, *amūbhi*.

87. *Na* is not [the substitute] for our [demonstrative pronoun] *amussa*. For *amussa*, *amūsaṃ*, and *amūsānaṃ*. From the rule "nāsmāssā," *nā* replaces *smā* and *ssa*; thus: *amunā*, *amumhā*, *amusmā*. In the locative: *amumhi*, *amusmiṃ*; and *amūsu*. In the feminine:
*asu*, *amū*, *amuyo*. *Amuṃ*, *amū*, *amuyo*. *Nā* [is used] for the singular forms of the nominative, dative, and accusative according to the rule "ssā vā te ti mā mūhī."
Or: *amussā*, *amuyā*, *amūhi*, *amūbhi*. *Amussā*, *amuyā*, *amūsaṃ*, *amūsānaṃ*. In the locative:
*amussaṃ*, *amussā*, *amuyaṃ*, *amuyā*, *amūsu*.
In the neuter:—

202. For *amu*, [the forms] *adu* and *aṃ* occur together with those [case endings]; in the neuter, *adu* or *aṃ* occurs. *Adu*: elision of the consonant (*silopa*), *amuṃ*. By the rule "jhalā vā," there is the substitution of *va*; thus *amūni* and *amū*. *Aduṃ*, *amuṃ*; *amūni*, *amū*. *Amunā*, etc., is the same as the masculine.
When the suffix *ka* is added by the rule "sakatte":...

130. In the case of "Ke vā amu eva amuko," because it is a secondary derivative (taddhita) formed with the suffix *ka* in the sense of identity (*sakattha*), the term "ekatthatāyaṃ" (in the state of having a single referent) applies;

furthermore, when the elision (*silopa*) has been performed, according to the principle that "in the absence of the cause, there is the absence of that which depends on the cause" (*nimittābhāve nemittikassābhāvo*), since the cause—the suffix *sissa*—is absent, [the dependent form is also absent].

In the expression “massā+mussā,” there is the removal (nivutti) of the letter *s* that ought to be applied; thus, by means of the alternative (*vikappa*) “or *ke*,” this [substitution] is undertaken for the sense of the letter *s* of *massa*.

That is to say: for the *massa* of *amussa*, *ke* may optionally become *sa*. Examples include: *asuko* / *amukā*, *asukā* / *amukā*, *asukaṃ* / *amukaṃ*, and so forth. [The interrogative pronoun *kiṃ* becomes *si*.]
198. Of *kiṃ*, what becomes of it in all the case-endings? *Sisso*, *ko*, *ke*. *Kaṃ*, *ke*. *Kena*, *kehi*, *kebhi*. 199.
*Ki* [is used] in the feminine (*nitthiyaṃ*) or in the neuter (*sasmiṃ*).
In the masculine (*anitthiyaṃ*), what [form] occurs after which [stems]? After *sa*, *kissa* and *kiṃ* occur. After *ka*, *kassa*; after *ke*, *kesaṃ* and *kesānaṃ*. After *kam*, *kamhā* and *kasmā*.

After *kim*, *kimhi*, *kismiṃ*, *kamhi*, and *kasmiṃ*; after *ke*, *kesu*. When the case endings follow *itthi*, the substitution of *kā* is made; because it ends in *a*, the addition of the suffix *āp* in the middle is not prohibited, resulting in *ā*, *kā*, and *kāyo*. *Kaṃ*, *kā*, *kāyo*, and so forth—all [forms] are likewise. In the neuter (*napuṃsake*)—
200. *Kiṃ* becomes *kiṃ* in the neuter when followed by *aṃ* or *su*.
When the word *kiṃ* is followed by *aṃ* or *su*, it becomes *kiṃ* in the neuter.

Because the substitution of *kā* is general, according to the maxim that "rules prescribed for specific cases preclude rules prescribed in a general manner," the substitution of *kā* is set aside by the substitution of *kiṃ*. Thus: *kiṃ*, *kāni*. *Kiṃ*.
"Which ones? Which?"—the suffixes *ena*, *ccādi*, and so forth have already been explained.
The word *eka* denotes number, similarity, otherness, and lack of a companion. When it denotes number, it ends in the singular; here, the word *eka* refers to that which is numbered (*saṃkhyeyya*).
In other cases, such as when denoting similarity and so forth, it may also end in the plural. [Examples: *eko*, *eke*; *ekā*, *ekā*, *ekāyo*.
*Ekaṃ*, *ekāni*, and so forth, are identical in all three genders. In the sense of equality: *eko vilāso dvinnaṃ kumārānaṃ* (one style of two princes);

*eke vaṇṇasaddā dvinnaṃ kumārānaṃ* (some words for color of two princes). In the sense of difference: *eko ācariyo evam āha* (one teacher said thus); *eke ācariyā evam āhaṃsu* (some teachers said thus). In the sense of being without a companion:

*eko va araññaṃ pavisitvā* (having entered the forest alone). The forms *eko*, *eke*; *ekā*, *ekā*, *ekāyo*; and *ekaṃ*, *ekāni*, and so forth, are identical in all three genders. However, in the case of *ssā*, *ssaṃ*, and *su*, by means of the suffix *ssa* and so on, there is the form *i*: *ekissā* or *ekāya* (genitive singular), *ekissaṃ* or *ekāyaṃ* or *ekāya* (locative singular).
Here, by way of self-respect (*attaparagāravavasena*), even for a single person, the plural number is desired by the world—as in "our king" (*amhākaṃ rañño*) or "some teachers" (*eke ācariyā*);

thus, by virtue of the rule of frequent occurrence (*bahulavidhānā*), it is formed using the plural ending itself. The words *tumha* and *amha* are devoid of gender (*aliṅga*); likewise are the words *ubha*, *kati*, and *dvi*, as well as the numbers beginning with *pañca* up to *aṭṭhārasa*. [The forms are: *tumha si*, *amha si*. 212. For *tumha*, there are *tuvaṃ*, *tvaṃ*, and *mamhi*.
*Amhi* and *simhi* are the forms for the second person (*tumha*) when accompanied by case endings; [the forms] are *tuvaṃ* and *tvaṃ*.
211. *Simha* and *haṃ* are the forms for the first person (*amha*) when accompanied by case endings; [the forms] are *ahaṃ*, *yevasve*, *ṭa*, *tu*, and *mhe*.

2,209. For the case-terminations *maya* and *masmā* of the word *amha*, there are optionally *maya* and *asmā* respectively, provided that the case-termination (*vibhatti*) follows. [Examples: *mayaṃ*, *amhe*.
227. In the locative singular (*amhi*), there are *taṃ*, *maṃ*, *tavaṃ*, and *mamaṃ*.
In place of the words *tumha* and *amha*, along with their case endings, *taṃ*, *maṃ*, *tavaṃ*, and *mamaṃ* occur respectively. That is: *taṃ*, *maṃ*, *tavaṃ*, *mamaṃ*. 231.

When the dative suffix *ya* occurs, in place of each of the words *tumha* and *amha*, along with their case endings, *ṅaṃ* or *ṅākaṃ* occur when *ya* is in the second case: *tumhaṃ*, *tumhākaṃ*, *tumhe*; *amhaṃ*, *amhākaṃ*, *amhe*.
228. *Tayā* and *mayā* [are the substitutes] for *nāsmāsu*;

*tayā* and *mayā* occur respectively for the forms *tuyhaṃ* and *amhaṃ* when they possess case endings. In the phrase "nāsmāsu," even though it is plural, two forms each occur for every word according to the sequence of the sounds (*saddakkamena*), regardless of the sequence of the case endings (*vibhattikkama*).
213. For *tayā* and *tayīnaṃ*, there is optionally *tvā*.
In the word *tumha*, the *t* of *tayātayīnaṃ* optionally becomes *tv*. [Examples: *tvayā* or *tayā*; *mayā*.
*Tumhehi* or *tumhebhi*; *amhehi* or *amhebhi*. 229.
*Tava*, *mama*, *tuyhaṃ*, and *mayhaṃ* are the substitutes for the words *tumha* and *amha* along with their case endings, respectively. [Examples: *tava* or *tuyhaṃ*; *mama* or *mayhaṃ*.
211. *Naṃsesva* [is used for] our (*asmākaṃ*) and mine (*mamaṃ*).
*Naṃsesva* occurs for *mhassa* when it has its case-ending (*savibhatti*), becoming *asmākaṃ* and *mamaṃ* respectively.
*Mamaṃ*. 230. *Ṅaṃ*, *ṅākaṃ*, *naṃ*, *mhi*.
In the case of the forms *tumhaṃ* and *amhaṃ*, which possess the suffix *-aṃ*, the substitutes *ṅaṃ* and *ṅākaṃ* respectively take their place. Thus: *tumhaṃ*, *tumhākaṃ*;
*amhaṃ*, *amhākaṃ*, *asmākaṃ*. In the *Kaccāyana*, this rule was commenced for the purpose of prescribing *-aṃ* for the singular;
however, here, by virtue of self-respect (*attagāravavasena*), the forms *tumhaṃ* and *amhaṃ* are established for the singular through the application of the "frequentative" (*bahula*) principle.
214. From *asmā* [comes] *tvam*;
from *yuṣmad* [comes] *tvam*, or it becomes *savitattissa*. From *tvad* [come] *tvayā* and *tayā*; [from *mad* comes] *mayā*. 226.
From *asmin* [comes] *tumhaṃ* and *naṃ*; [from *yuṣmad* come] *tayi* and *mayi*.
In the case of the forms *tumha* and *amha*, when followed by the suffixes *sum* and *hi*, *tayi* and *mayi* respectively take their place. Thus: *tvayi* (for *tumhe*), *tayi*; *mayi*.
[The form] *tumhesu* [is used]. 203. Regarding *sumhā* and *mhassā*:

after the stem *amha*, *asmā* optionally occurs in place of *sumhi*. Thus: *asmāsu* or *amhesu*. The characteristic of these [pronouns], beginning with *sabba*, is that they refer either to what has already been mentioned or to what is yet to be mentioned.
232. *Apādādo padate kavākyeti*: This is a governing rule (*adhikāra*).

Here, "foot" (*pāda*) refers to one-fourth of a verse (*gāthā*); therefore, in the phrase “*tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappakan*,” the substitution of *vo* for *tumhehi* does not occur. Here, the word "foot" (*pada*) is stated by its own inherent nature (*sabhāvato*):
[it arises from] space, wind, and the body.
The sound, as it issues forth, attains the state of a process;
when well-restrained at its various points of articulation,
it attains the state of a phoneme, and that indeed becomes a word.

Because they have been so stated, each individual phoneme (vaṇṇa) is called "sound" (sadda); a collection of those phonemes is a word (pada), and a collection of those words is a sentence (vākya). For it has been said:
"We consider that which is fully stretched out to be a word, and that which follows from it to be a sentence;
by way of metaphorical designation (upacāra), one should not abandon the fact that these are denoted by the term 'sound' (sadda)."
And as for that word—The word is said to be fourfold: consisting of nouns, verbs, prefixes, and particles;
for those who know it is thus: "the horse indeed runs."
And regarding that statement:
"A collection of words consisting of a single verb may be a sentence provided it possesses a kāraka"—so it has been said.
Therefore, it is also stated: "A word ends in a case-suffix; a collection of words is a sentence."

233. In a single sentence, the forms *vo* and *no* optionally replace the case-inflected words *tumha* and *amha* respectively, provided they follow a word ending in *yo*, *naṃ*, *hi*, *su*, or *pañcamī*, or are situated at the beginning of a line (*pādādo*).
For example: *gāmaṃ vo gaccheyyātha* (you should go to the village), or *gāmaṃ tumhe gaccheyyātha*.
We would go to the village; let the village come to us. Having abandoned you, I shall go; do not be distressed for us. It is given to you;

it is given to your [selves]. It is given to us; it is given to our [selves]. I am pleased with you by nature; I am pleased with your [selves]. The Blessed One is our Teacher; he is our Teacher. It was done by you; it was done by your [selves]. It was done by us; it was done by our [selves].

234. *Te* and *me* are the substitutes for *tumha* and *amha*, respectively, when these words stand within a single sentence together with their case endings (*savibhatti*), provided that *dassā* (the dative-locative plural ending) follows immediately after them. For example:
*kataṃ te* (done by you), *kataṃ tayā*; *kataṃ me* (done by me), *kataṃ mayā*.

It is given to you, it is given for you (*te*). It is given to me, it is given for me (*me*). Wealth is yours (*te*), wealth is for you (*tava*). Wealth is mine (*me*), wealth is for me (*mama*). 237.

Furthermore, when used in conjunction with *vā*, *ha*, *e*, or *va*, and when joined with particles such as *ca* and so forth, the forms *vo* and *no* do not replace *tumha*, nor do *te* and *me* replace *amha*. For example: "We go, both you and we" (*gacchāma tumhe ca mayañca*); "he sees... (*passati*).
"Both you and we," "done by both you and us," "it is given to both you and us," "wealth for both you and us";
"both by you and by me," "it is given to both you and me," "wealth for both you and me. Even in such applications of speech.
235. In the case of subsequent reference (anvādesa):

In the context of what has already been mentioned (*kathita*) and what is being mentioned again (*anukathita*), the substitutes for the words *tumha* and *amha* occur invariably due to their re-mention (*punabbidhāna*). For example: "The village is your possession;
moreover, the country is your possession" (*gāmo tumhaṃ pariggaho, atho janapado vo pariggaho*).

In the case of re-mention (*anvādesa*), because the word *atha* occurs twice, it is stated that [the substitution] is "invariable" (*nicca*). The word *atha*, because it mentions again that which has already been mentioned, indicates re-mention (*anvādesa*).

236. Optionally, when preceded by *sa* or when preceded by an existing [word] ending in the first case (*paṭhamanta*), the substitutes *tumha* and *amha* may optionally occur for subsequent instances of *tumhākaṃ* in an anvādesa (subsequent reference). For example:
*gāme paṭo tumhākaṃ atho nagare kambalo vo*, or *atho nagare kambalo tumhākaṃ*. The word *atha* is used because there are two turns of speech in this subsequent reference.
What is the meaning of *vikappa* with *sapubba*? "The cloth is yours, and also the blanket is yours. What is the meaning of *paṭhama* with *anta*?
"The cloth is yours in the city, and also the blanket is yours in the village.
238. [The suffix *na* is used] after a verb having the sense of seeing, except for the act of looking.

When the word *ālo* is employed in the sense of seeing (*dassana*), excluding the verbal root *vac*, the substitutions *tumha* and *amha* do not occur. For example: *Gāmo tumhe uddissa āgato* (The village has come for you), *Gāmo amhe uddissa āgato* (The village has come for us). Why is it specified "excluding [the sense of] looking" (*anālocane*)? Consider: *Gāmo vo āloceti* (The village looks at you), *Gāmo no āloceti* (The village looks at us). 239.

An address (*āmantaṇaṃ*) that precedes [the form] appears as if it were non-existent, even when it exists before the scope of the substitutions *tumha* and *amha*. For example: *Devadatta tava pariggaho* (O Devadatta, this is your property). Why is it called "address"? Consider: *Kambalo te pariggaho* (The blanket is your property).

240. When a general term follows another general term in apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*), that general term [in the vocative] does not become as if non-existent when there is a single referent (*ekattha*); for example: *māṇavaka jaṭilaka te pariggaho*. Even though the subsequent [term] is elided, the substitution occurs based on the preceding one.
241. Or, when there are many [referents].
When used in the plural, an address of general application (*sāmaññavacana*) does not function as if it were non-existent when combined with another word in a single compound.

Because it is stated that "an undertaking [of a rule] occurs when [the meaning] is already established, or for the sake of an alternative (*vikappa*) being led forward," this [rule] has the sense of an alternative. Examples:
*brāhmaṇā guṇavanto tumhākaṃ pariggaho* (virtuous Brahmins are your dependents), or *brāhmaṇā guṇavanto vo pariggaho*.

The words *ubha* and *kati* end in the plural number. Regarding the rule “*ubha* + *go* = *ṭo*,” the suffix *ṭo* is applied to the word *ubha*, resulting in *ubho*. How is it that [the form] “*ubhayo vasemase*” occurs? It is because the letter *y* is inserted before the suffix *ṭo*.
Thus: *ubho*. 59. *Suhisv-ubhassa*:
The substitution of *su* and *hi* occurs for *ubha*. Thus: *ubhohi*, *ubhobhi*.
50. *Ubhinnaṃ*:
The suffix *inaṃ* is substituted for the word *ubho*. [Examples: *ubhinnaṃ*, *ubhosu*.
168. *Ṭi* from *kati*.

In what [words] does *ṭi* occur? In *kati*, *kati*. The substitution of *ṭi* is for the purpose of excluding the long vowel when the elision of *yo* (*yolopa*) would otherwise apply after *jhata*. [Examples: *katīhi*, *katībhi*; by the rule "of *bahu* and *kati*," there is *nuka*: *katinnaṃ*, *katīsu*. 1.54.

In distributive repetition (*vicchā*) and in the case of *abhikkhañña*, there are two forms. Distributive repetition (*vicchā*) is the desire to extend [an action, quality, or substance] over many things.
They water tree after tree; every village is delightful; there is drinking water in every village.
Repeatedly = merit upon merit; cooks and cooks; cooks thoroughly and cooks thoroughly. 1,55.
Elision of *syādi* (the suffixes beginning with *si*) following a preceding *e* or *o*.

In the doubling (*dvitta*) of a single word, there is the elision of the case endings (*syādi*) of the preceding [word]. "Of a single word" means of each individual [word] when doubled. How is it that in the expression “matthakamatthakena” (head to head) there is the elision of the preceding case ending?

It is by means of a separation of rules (*yogavibhāga*); and through such a separation of rules, the desired result is established. 1.56. In the sense of reciprocity (*vītihāra*), words beginning with *sabba* become doubled. There is also the elision of the case endings of the preceding [word]. For example: *aññassa aññassa bhojakā* becomes *aññamaññassa bhojakā*; likewise, *itarītarassa*.
1,57. Up to the point of awakening, there is agitation;
the rapid utterance of words that indicate the cause of danger is "agitation. When that exists, as many sounds as are necessary for that meaning to be understood are employed:
*sappo sappo sappo* (snake, snake, snake), *bujjhassu bujjhassu bujjhassu* (awake, awake, awake).
"The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is split! The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is split!"—
a wise person should employ reduplication (āmreḍita) in cases of fear, anger, praise, haste, excitement, wonder, laughter, sorrow, and joy.
The Section on Numbers (Saṅkhyākaṇḍa).
Now, the words for numbers are being explained. From *eka* (one) up to eighteen, these are words denoting that which is to be numbered (*saṅkhyeyya-vacana*).

From twenty onwards, they are words denoting the number itself (*saṅkhyā-vacana*) in such expressions as “twenty of the monks” (*bhikkhūnaṃ vīsatī*); however, in such expressions as “twenty monks” (*vīsati bhikkhavo*), they are words denoting that which is to be numbered. The word *eka*...
It is stated as such among the words beginning with *sabba*. From two (*dvi*) up to eighteen, they take only plural endings. 219.

In the case of the *yo* ending, for the two [words], there are *duve* and *dve*; for the word *dvi* together with its case-ending, *duve* and *dve* occur respectively. [Examples: *duve dve*, *duve dve*, *dvīhi dvībhi*.
220. For *duvi*, before the suffix *naṃ*, there is optionally [the form] *naṃ*.
For the word *dvi* together with its case-ending, *duvinnaṃ* occurs optionally. *Duvinnaṃ*—except otherwise:
47. Before the suffix *naṃ*, there is *nu* for the seventeen words beginning with *dvā*.

The augment *n* occurs before the case-ending *nam* after the numbers from twelve (*dvādīnaṃ*) up to seventeen (*sattarasannaṃ*). The letter *u* is for the purpose of pronunciation (*uccāraṇattha*), and the letter *k* is for the purpose of indicating the final portion (*antāvayavattha*).

Here, if the augment *n* were merely the initial portion of the case-ending, then according to the principle that "augments which have become subordinate to something are included by the mention of that thing," the augment *n* would also be included by the mention of that [ending].
Consequently, there would be the undesirable consequence (*pasaṅge*) of lengthening [the vowel] in the form *sunamhi*.
Since there is no state of ending in a vowel (*sarantatā*) when [the word] is naturally a member of a compound, there is no long vowel.
*Dvinnaṃ*, *dvīsu*. 207. *Pume tayo+cattāro*:

In the masculine, in the locative case (*yo*), for the forms *ti* and *cattāro* along with their case-endings, *tayo* and *cattāro* occur respectively in the masculine gender. *Tayo*, *tayo*, *tīhi*, *tībhi*.
49. After the word *ti*, the forms *ṇṇam* and *ṇṇam* occur in place of the neuter singular suffix *nam*. [Thus: *tiṇṇam*, *tiṇṇam*, and *tīsu*.
In the feminine:
205. *Tisso* and *catasso* [are the forms] in the locative case (*yoṃhi*) when accompanied by case-endings;
for the words *ti* and *cattāri* when joined with case-endings, *tisso* and *catasso* respectively occur in the feminine. [Examples: *tisso*, *tisso*, *tīhi*, *tībhi*. 204.
In the accusative case (*naṃmhi*), for the words *ti* and *cattāri* in the feminine, [the forms are] *tissa* and *catassā*.

In the case of *naṃ* [as a suffix], *tissa* and *catassā* occur respectively after the three and four [neuter stems] ending in *naṃ*, when followed by the fourth case (*catutthī*) or the sixth case (*chaṭṭhī*).

The term *naṃhi* is a general designation for the fourth and sixth cases; it is not intended to exclude the word *naṃ*. "Respectively" (*yathākkamaṃ*) refers to the two preceding words. This applies to similar cases as well. *Tissannaṃ* means "in the three. 206. Three and four [are used] in the neuter.

In the neuter gender, for the three and four case endings (*savibhattīnaṃ*) [of the plural], there are respectively three and four forms. In the masculine gender, it is *tīṇi*, *tīṇi*, *tīhi*, and so forth.
Regarding *catu*: 208. *Caturo vā catussa*.
In the masculine gender, for the word *cattāro* when it has the case-ending *yo*, there is optionally the form *caturo*. Thus: *caturo* or *cattāro*.

How is it that in the phrase “*caturo nimitte nāddasāsi*” (you did not see four signs), the form is established? It is established through a reversal of gender (*liṅgavipallāsa*); the meaning is “four signs. Reversal is threefold:
reversal of gender, reversal of number (*vacanavipallāsa*), and reversal of case-ending (*vibhattivipallāsa*). [The forms] *catūhi*, *catūbhi*; [the genitive] *catunnaṃ*; [the locative] *catūsu*.
In the feminine: *itthiyam* (in her), *catasso* (four), *catassobhi* (by four), *catassannam* (of four), *catassannam* (to four), *catassu* (in four).
In the neuter: *cattāri* (four), *cattāri* (four), *catūhi* or *catūbhi* (by four), and so forth, just as in the masculine.
169. [The suffix] *ṭa* [is applied] after the fourteen [words] beginning with *pañca*.

“*Sutte liṅgavacanamattan*” (in the sutta, it is merely for the sake of gender and number)—this is stated according to the grammatical method (*ñāya*) as *ṭa*. The suffix *ṭa* occurs after numbers beginning with five and ending with fourteen. [Examples: *pañca*, *pañca*.

The prescription of *ṭa* is for the purpose of replacing the *ṭā* and *ṭena* suffixes. 90. *Pañcādīnaṃ cuddasannaṃ su na hisva hoti*: After the fourteen numbers beginning with five, *su* becomes *na hisva*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule regarding short and long vowels. It is called an exception because it sets aside (*bādheti*) the general rule.

This is an exception (*apavāda*). Therefore, according to the principle that "general rules (*ussagga*) apply to spheres other than those of exceptions," the general rules "for *su* and *hi*" and "for *su* and *naṃhi*" do not enter the sphere of the exception "for the fourteen beginning with *pañca*," because they are common [to all]. The same applies to the subsequent rules:
"in the fifth case for another" and "for *ādi*. [Examples: *pañcahi*, *pañcabhi*, *pañcannaṃ*; *pañcannaṃ*.
In the case of *pañcasu*. Likewise, from six up to eighteen.

When the compound *cattasamāse* is formed as "four and ten" (*cattha*), meaning "ten plus one," or when the third-case compound *tatiyāsamāse* is formed as "ten plus one" (*amādī*), the case-ending elision occurs due to "unity of meaning" (*ekatthatāya*). The same applies in the following cases.
3,102. *Ekaṭṭhānam ā-* [elision of the case-ending].
A single instance occurs; ten is the limit.
3,103. *Ra* optionally replaces *saṃkhyāta*;
after a numeral, *ra* optionally replaces the following *da*. And that [occurs] while the rule "in the fifth case, for another" is in effect.
“Ādissa” means [the substitution] occurs only for the letter *da*. *Ekārasa* becomes *ekādasa*. *Ekārasāhi* becomes *ekādasāhi*. *Ekārasannaṃ* becomes *ekādasannaṃ*. *Ekārasasu* becomes *ekādasasu*.
Likewise, *ekādasa* and so forth. 3.94. Before a numeral beginning with *sata*, [the final vowel] becomes *ā* when there is no other meaning [i.e., no possessive sense].
When a numeral is followed by a subsequent word (*uttarapada*), the doubling (*dvis*) occurs, provided it does not mean "not existing" (*asatāda*) and is not used in another sense.
Because its gender is inherent (*āviṭṭhaliṅga*), the qualifier remains in that same gender when the numeral is the subsequent word. [The types of compounds are:
pure (*suddha*), mixed (*missa*), variegated (*saṃkiṇṇa*), and subordinate (*upasajjana*).
Or else, when the [gender] is clearly manifest, the gender is analyzed in six ways.
Herein, according to the sequence: "tree," "creeper," and "leaf" are pure (suddha). "Jar," "jar," "thunderbolt," "thunderbolt," "feeling," and "feeling" are mixed (missa).
"Bank," "bank," and "bank" are commingled (saṃkiṇṇa). "White cloth," "white cloth," and "white garment" are [also examples].

The subordinate element (*upasajjana*). "The king is the refuge" (*rājā saraṇaṃ*) and "virtue is the measure" (*guṇo pamāṇaṃ*) are *āviṭṭha* (informed). "You, I, how many, five" (*tuvaṃ ahaṃ kati pañca*) are *abyatta* (unexpressed).
Thus the gender (*liṅga*) is to be understood.
Twelve. 3,98. Forty-two.
After *dvi*, [the suffix] *bā* or *vā* occurs, or [it becomes] *cattālīsa*; after *dve*, it is not otherwise. After *rā*, *se*, or *bā*, [the suffix] *lasa* occurs. 3.95.
When a numeral follows as a subsequent member (*uttarapada*), the *t* of *ti* becomes *e*, provided it does not mean "hundred" or other such cases.
3,104. After *catur*, *ḷ* and *r* are substituted for the *da* of another word; *ḷ* and *ro* [are also substituted]. Thus: *teḷasa*, *terasa*.
3,100. For *catuṣ*, *cu* and *co* [are substituted] before *dasa*.
When *cu* or *da* follow, they become *cu* and *ca*. In the case of doubling, [the forms] are *cuddasa*, *coddasa*, and *catuddasa*.
(3,99) In the words *vīsati* and *dasa*, the word *pañca* becomes *paṇṇa* or *panna*.
In the remaining following words, *pañca* becomes *paṇṇa* or *panna* respectively. Thus: *pannarasa* and *pañcadasa*.

3,101. *Cha* and *sa*, when followed by *so*, undergo the substitution (*mādeso*) of *sso*. Thus: *soḷasa* becomes *sorasa*; *sattarasa* becomes *sattadasa*. By the rule "when preceded by *eka* or *aṭṭha*," *ā* is substituted; thus *aṭṭhārasa* becomes *aṭṭhādasa*. Furthermore, regarding the compound *ūnā ca sā vīsati ca* ("less than twenty"): first, a descriptive determinative compound (*visesanasa-māso*) is formed according to the rule "a qualifier [is compounded] with that which it qualifies when they have a single referent.

Then, because the word is feminine but has a masculine base, and since it is a single referent, the feminine form is replaced by the masculine according to the rule "in the feminine, a word whose masculine base has been stated becomes masculine when it is a single referent. Having thus made it masculine, the phrase *ekena ūnā vīsati* ("twenty less by one") forms a third-case compound (*tatiyāsamāso*), resulting in *ekūnavīsati*.

The forms beginning with *vīsati* up to *aṇavuti* are feminine singular nouns. *Bho ekūnavīsati*. *Ekūnavīsatiṃ*. *Ekūnavīsatyā*, *ekūnavīsatiyā*. *Ekūnavīsatyaṃ*, *ekūnavīsatiyaṃ*, *ekūnavīsatyā*, *ekūnavīsatiyā*. This is the same as for *mati*. In the same way:

*vīsati*, *ekavīsati*, *dvāvīsati*, *bāvīsati*, *tevīsati*, *catuvīsatippabhutayo* (twenty-four, etc.). With the substitution of *paṇṇa* [for *pañca*], there is *paṇṇavīsati*, *pañcavīsati*. In the same way: *chabbīsati*, *sattavīsati*, *aṭṭhavīsati*.

*Ekena ūnā tiṃsati* means "thirty less one," that is, twenty-nine (*ekūnatiṃsati*) or twenty-nine (*ekūnatiṃsā*). In the instrumental case, it is *ekūnatiṃsāya*. [The forms] *ekūnatiṃsāya*, *ekūnatiṃsāya*, *ekūnatiṃsāya*, and *ekūnatiṃsāyaṃ* follow.

Thus are the forms for thirty (*tiṃsati*), thirty (*tiṃsā*), and twenty-nine (*ekūnatiṃsā*). However, when the syllable *s* of the word *tiṃsā* is elided, by the rule "the vowel becomes long" (*dīghasso*) through the division of the grammatical rule (*yogavibhāga*), the short vowel remains:
*tiṃsa*. When the nasal *ṃ* (niggahīta) is inserted, it is *tiṃsaṃ*. The forms beginning with *bhotiṃse* and so forth are likewise only masculine.
In the case of *cattālīsa* and so forth, it is exactly the same according to what is applicable. In the dual (*dvitte*), there are *ekattiṃsati* and *ekattiṃsā*.
In the short dual (*rassadvitte*), there are *dvattiṃsati* and *dvattiṃsa*. Likewise, there are *tettiṃsati*, *tettiṃsā*, and so on, up to *ekūnacattālīsati* and *ekūnacattālīsā*.

For the word *cattālīsa* in the nominative singular (*simhi*), there are *cattārīsā*, *cattālīsā*, and *cattālīsaṃ*; in the vocative, there is *bho cattālīse*, and so forth. The same applies to *ekacattālīsā*.
3.97. After *dvi* (two), *sā* (sixty), and *asati* (eighty), the *ā* of *catālīsā* (forty) becomes *e* or *ā*. Thus: *dvecattālīsā*, *dvecattālīsa*, *dvecattālīsaṃ*;
likewise, *dvācattālīsa*, etc. [Similarly: *dvecattārīsā*, *dvecattārīsa*, *dvecattārīsaṃ*; likewise, *dvācattārīsā*.
“Dvācattārīsa” and so forth. [The forms] “cattālīsati,” “ekacattālīsati,” “dvecattālīsati,” and “dvācattālīsati,” and so on, constitute the nineteenth [section]. 3,98. “Cattālīsādo vā”:
after the word *cattālīsa*, the suffix *tissa* optionally occurs in the sense of “not being six” (*asatāda*), but not in other senses. [Examples: *tecattālīsā*, *tecattālīsa*, *tecattālīsaṃ*.
"Bho tecattālīse" and so forth occurs [in the vocative]. Likewise, "ticattālīsā," "tecattārīsā," "ticattārīsā," and so forth;
"tecattālīsati," "tecattālīsati," and so forth, as before.
Similarly, "catucattālīsā," "pañcacattālīsā," "catucattālīsati," "pañcacattālīsati," and so forth, up to "ekūnapaññāsā."
*Paññāsā*, *paññāsa*, *paññāsaṃ*, and so forth. Likewise: *dvepaññāsā*, *dvāpaññāsā*, *dvipaññāsā*, *dvepaṇṇāsā*, *dvāpaṇṇāsā*, *dvipaṇṇāsā*;
*tepaññāsā*, *tipaññāsā*, *tipaññāsaṃ*, *tepaṇṇāsā*, *tipaṇṇāsā*;
*catupaṇṇāsā*, *pañcapaṇṇāsā*, and so on, up to fifty-nine (*ekūnasaṭṭhi*).
Thus: sixty-one, sixty-two, sixty-three, sixty-four, sixty-five, and so forth, up to sixty-nine;

seventy, seventy-one, seventy-two, seventy-three, seventy-four, seventy-five; seventy-six, seventy-seven, seventy-eight, seventy-nine, and up to seventy-nine; eighty, eighty-one, eighty-two, eighty-three, eighty-four, eighty-five, eighty-six, eighty-seven, eighty-eight, and up to eighty-nine.
Eighty, eighty-one, eighty-two, eighty-three, eighty-four, eighty-five, and so on up to eighty-nine;
ninety, ninety-one, ninety-two, ninety-three, ninety-four, ninety-five, and so on up to ninety-nine—these are neuter gender nouns in the singular number.

*Sataṃ*, O sir, *sata satā*, *sataṃ*, *sataṃ*. *Satena* [is used] in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*). *Satassa*, *satā*, *satamhā*, *satasmā*; *satassa*, *sate*, *satamhi*, *satasmiṃ*. Thus, from one hundred onwards up to a thousand.

*Koṭi*, *pakoṭi*, *koṭippakoṭi*, *akkhobhiṇiyo*—these are feminine gender nouns ending in the plural number. However, when there is a division into groups (*vaggabhede*), even for all these numbers the plural is indeed used, as in: “twenty-two sets of Buddha’s teeth,” or “three sets of twenty day-units (*dinaghaṭikā*)” and so forth.
Ten tens are called a hundred; ten hundreds are called a thousand; ten thousands are a *nahuta*; ten *nahutas* are a *lakkha*, which is also called a hundred thousand.
A hundred *lakkhas* are a *koṭi*; a hundred *koṭis* of *lakkhas* are a *pakoṭi*; a hundred *pakoṭis* of *lakkhas* are a *koṭippakoṭi*. In this same manner:
a *nahuta*, a *ninnahuta*, an *akkhobhiṇī*, a *bindu*, an *abbuda*, a *nirabbuda*, an *ahahaṃ*, an *ababaṃ*, an *aṭaṭaṃ*, and a *sogaṇḍikaṃ*.
The *uppala*, *kumuda*, *puṇḍarīka*, *paduma*, *kathāna*, *mahākathāna*, and *asaṅkhyeyya* should be understood as being multiplied by one hundred thousand times in successive order.
Thus, from one position to the next, it is considered to be multiplied by one hundred thousand.
The twenty [prefixes], beginning with *koṭi*, follow their respective order.

Now, that which is called "innumerable" (*asaṃkhyā*) is also called "indeclinable" (*abyaya*). It is twofold: beginning with *pā-* and beginning with *cā-*, namely prepositions (*upasagga*) and particles (*nipāta*).

*Pa*, *parā*, *apa*, *saṃ*, *anu*, *ava*, *o*, *ni*, *du*, *vi*, *adhi*, *api*, *ati*, *su*, *u*, *abhi*, *pati*, *pari*, *upa*, *ā*—these twenty are the prefixes (*pāda*). For the prefixes are indicators (*jotaka*), not denoters (*vācaka*).

In this context, the prefix *pa-* is used in the senses of manner (*pakāra*), initial action (*ādikamma*), excellence (*padhāna*), inclusion (*antobhāva*), separation (*viyoga*), devotion (*tappara*), intensity (*bhusattha*), arising (*sambhava*), satiety (*titti*), clarity (*anāvila*), aspiration (*patthana*), and so forth.
For example: in the sense of manner—as in *paññā* (wisdom); in initial action—as in *vippakataṃ* (half-done); in excellence—as in *paṇītaṃ* (excellent);
in inclusion—as in *pakkhittaṃ* (placed within), where *khittaṃ* means throwing and *pakkhittaṃ* means making internal; it expresses the meaning of the verbal root.
Because it is sublated. For it has been stated:
"One [prefix] sublates the meaning of the verbal root, another follows it; yet another qualifies that very same [meaning].
Thus, the functions of prefixes are threefold."

And here, these prefixes—“anuruddhakā me saṅgāmayuddhe” (my men were victorious in the battle)—are said to qualify the meaning of the verbal root (*dhātu*). [Examples are: *viyoge* (in the sense of separation): *pavāsī* (one who has gone abroad); *tappare* (in the sense of being intent on):

*pācariyo* (a teacher); *bhusatthe* (in the sense of intensity): *pavuddhakāyo* (one whose body has grown large); *sambhave* (in the sense of origin): *himavantā gaṅgā pabhavati* (the Gaṅgā originates from the Himālayas); *tittiyaṃ* (in the sense of satiety): *pahūtamannaṃ* (abundant food);
*anāvile* (in the sense of non-turbidity): *pasannamudakaṃ* (clear water); *patthanaṃ* (in the sense of aspiration): *paṇihitaṃ* (directed).

*Parā-iti* occurs in the senses of decline (*parihāni*), defeat (*parājaya*), going (*gati*), and stroking (*āmasana*), etc. For example: in the sense of decline, *parābhavo*; in the sense of defeat, *parājito*; in the sense of going, *parāyanaṃ*; in the sense of exertion, *parakkamati*; in the sense of stroking, *aṅgassa parāmasanaṃ*.

*Apā-iti* occurs in the senses of departing (*apagata*), reproach (*garaḥa*), avoidance (*vajjana*), honoring (*pūjā*), and offending (*padussana*), etc. For example: in the sense of departing, *apamāno apeto*; in the sense of reproach, *apagabbho*; in the sense of avoidance, *apasālāya āyanti vāṇijā*; in the sense of honoring, *vuddhāpacāyī*; in the sense of offending, *aparajjhanti*.

*Saṃ* has the meanings of: conjunction (*samodhāna*), rightness (*sammāsama*), all-encompassing state (*samantabhāva*), meeting (*saṃgata*), conciseness (*saṃkhepa*), intensity (*bhusattha*), together with (*saha+ppattha*), being directed toward the source (*pabhavābhimukhabhāva*), arrangement (*vidhāna*), repetition (*punappuna*), doing (*karaṇa*), and in words such as *samiddha*. For example: in the sense of conjunction—*sandhi*;
in the sense of rightness—*samādhi*, *sampayutta*; in the sense of all-encompassing state—*saṃkiṇṇaṃ*, *samullapanā*; in the sense of meeting—*saṅgamo*.
*Saṃ* has the sense of "in brief" in *saṃkhitta*, the sense of "intense" in *sāra*, the sense of "together" in *saṃvāsa*, the sense of "worthless" in *samaggha*, the sense of "origin" in *sambhava*,
and the sense of "facing" in *sammukha*. It has the sense of "gathering" in *saṃgaṇhāti*, the sense of "restraint" in *saṃvuta*, the sense of "repeated action" in *sandhāvati*,
and the sense of "perfection" in *sampanna*.

*Anu* is used in the senses of: following (*anugata*), uninterrupted (*anupacchinna*), posteriority (*pacchāttha*), intensity (*bhusattha*), similarity (*sādissa*), inferiority (*hīna*), thirdness (*tatiyattha*), characteristic (*lakkhaṇa*), pillar-like statement (*thambhūtakkhāna*), portion (*bhāga*), and distribution (*vicchā*).
In the sense of following: *anveti*. In the sense of being uninterrupted: *anusayo*. In the sense of posteriority: *anuratham*. In the sense of intensity: *anuratto*.

In the sense of similarity: *anurūpam*. In the sense of inferiority: *anusāriputtam paññavanto* (those wise ones who follow Sāriputta). In the sense of thirdness: *nadiṃ manvavasitā senā* (the army has encamped along the river).

Lightning flashes along the tree (*lakkhaṇa*). In the sense of expressing a state of being (*itthambhūtakhyāna*): Devadatta is kind toward his mother (*mātaram anu*). In the sense of a portion (*bhāga*):

let that which may belong to me here be given to me (*mam anu*). In the sense of proximity (*vicchāya*): the moon shines along every tree (*rukkham rukkham anu*). The prefix *anu* is used in the senses of:

lower part (*adhobhāga*), separation (*viyoga*), contempt (*paribhava*), knowledge (*jānana*), purification (*suddhi*), certainty (*nicchaya*), region (*desa*), theft (*theyya*), and so forth. In the sense of the lower part: "with eyes cast downward" (*avakkhittacakkhu*).

In the sense of separation: *avakokilaṃ* (the forest [without cuckoos]); in the sense of contempt: *avajānanaṃ*, *avamannati*; in the sense of knowing: *avagacchati*. In the sense of purity: *vodānaṃ* (etymological derivation);
in the sense of certainty: *avadhāraṇaṃ*; in the sense of place: *avakāso*; in the sense of theft: *avahāro*.

The prefix *o-* is seen in the senses of descending (*oroharaṇa*), taking out (*nīharaṇa*), purity (*suddhi*), and so forth. In the sense of descending: *pāsādā orohati* (he descends from the palace); in the sense of taking out: *omukkapāhano* (one who has taken off his sandals); in the sense of purity: *odātaṃ* (white).

*Ni* is used in the senses of remainder (*nissesa*), gone out (*niggata*), taking out (*nīharaṇa*), entering within (*antopavesanā*), non-existence (*abhāva*), prohibition (*nisedhana*), emerged (*nikkhanta*), determination of manifestation (*pātubhāvāvadhāraṇa*), analysis (*vibhajana*), comparison (*upama*), supporting (*upadhāraṇā*), conclusion (*avasāna*), skill (*cheka*), and taking out or covering (*nīharaṇāvaraṇādi*).

Examples: In the sense of "remainder": *nirutti*. In the sense of "gone out": *nikkileso* (free from defilement), *niyyāti* (goes forth). In the sense of "taking out": *niddhāraṇaṃ* (selection/exclusion). In the sense of "entering within":
*nikhāto* (planted/deeply fixed). In the sense of "non-existence": *nimmakkhikaṃ* (free from flies). In the sense of "prohibition": *nivāreti* (he prevents).
In the sense of departing, it is *nibbāna*; in the sense of manifestation, *nimmita*; in the sense of restriction, *nicchayo*; in the sense of analysis, *niddeso*.

In the sense of comparison, *nidassanaṃ*; in the sense of supporting, *nisāmanaṃ*; at the end, *niṭṭhitaṃ*; in the sense of being clever, *nipuṇo*; in the sense of taking out, *nīharati*—here the vowel is long. In the sense of obstruction, *nīvaraṇaṃ*.
*Duti* refers to lack of beauty, contemptible success, difficulty, ugliness, and so forth. In the sense of lack of beauty, *duggandho*.

In the sense of non-existence, *dubbhikkhaṃ* (famine); in the sense of contemptible, *dukkataṃ* (wrong-doing). In the sense of lack of prosperity, *dussassaṃ* (bad harvest); in the sense of difficulty, *dukkaraṃ* (hard to do); in the sense of deformity, *dubbaṇṇo* (ugly) and *dummukho* (ill-favored).

The prefix *vi-* [is used] in the senses of distinction (*visesa*), variety (*vividha*), opposition (*viruddha*), disappearance (*vigata*), separation (*viyoga*), deformity (*virūpatā*), and so forth. In the sense of distinction: *vimutti* (liberation), *visiṭṭho* (distinguished). In the sense of variety: *vimati* (doubt). In the sense of opposition: *vivādo* (dispute). In the sense of disappearance: *vimalaṃ* (stainless). In the sense of separation: *vippayutto* (dissociated). In the sense of deformity: *virūpo* (deformed).

*Adhi* is used in the senses of superiority (*adhika*), lordship (*issara*), pervasion (*paribhāva*), overcoming (*adhibhavana*), meditation (*ajjhāya*), resolution (*adhiṭṭhāna*), attainment (*pāpuṇana*), and so forth.
In the sense of superiority: *adhisīlaṃ*. In the sense of lordship: *adhipati*. In the sense of [belonging to] Brahmadatta: *adhi brahmadatte pañcālā*. In the sense of being above:

*adhirohati*. In the sense of lying upon: *pathaviṃ adhisessati*. In the sense of overcoming: *adhibhavati*. In the sense of recitation: *byākaraṇaṃ adhīte*. In the sense of resolution: [he resolves] an earthquake, etc. (*bhūmikampādiṃ*).
*Adhiṭṭhāti*: resolve; *adhimokkho*: determination; *pāpuṇane*: one attains a mass of wealth (*bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati*). *Api*:

[is used] in the sense of esteem (*sambhāvanā*), regard (*apekkhā*), conjunction (*samuccaya*), censure (*garaha*), inquiry (*pañha*), and so forth. In the sense of esteem: "Even among divine pleasures";
in the sense of regard: "He might even go through Mount Meru"; in the sense of conjunction: "This phenomenon is also indeterminate" (*aniyato*); and so on.
"An arahant, having taken even the edge and even the fibers of the edge—even in our reproach, O wise one—even in the question, Venerable Sir, you have received alms.

*Ati*: from *ati-kkamaṇa*, *ati-kkanta*, *ati-saya*; in the sense of "excessive," etc. In the sense of surpassing: *atirocati amhehi* (he shines beyond us). In the sense of transcended: *atīta*. In the sense of transcended: *accantaṃ*. In the sense of excellence: *atikusala*. In the sense of intensity: *atikodha*, *ativuddhi*.

*Su-* occurs in the senses of beautiful (*sobhana*), well (*suṭṭhu*), rightly (*sammā*), prosperity (*samiddhi*), happiness (*sukha*), and so forth. In the sense of "beautiful": *sugandha* (fragrant). In the senses of "well" and "rightly": *sugata*—one who has gone well (*suṭṭhu gata*) is a *sugata*, and one who has gone rightly (*sammā gata*) is also a *sugata*.

In the sense of "prosperity": *subhikkhaṃ* (an abundance of food). In the sense of "happiness": *sukara* (easy to do). *U-* occurs in the senses of rising (*uggata*), upward action (*uddhakamma*), exertion (*padhāna*), separation (*viyoga*), arising (*sambhava*), attainment of self (*attalābha*), power (*satti*), description of form (*sarūpakathana*), and so forth.

In the sense of "rising": *uggacchati* (it rises). In the sense of "upward action": *āsanā uṭṭhito* (risen from his seat), or *ukkhepo* (lifting up). In the sense of "exertion": *uttama* (supreme), *lokuttara* (supramundane).
In separation, it is *ubbhāsita*; in arising, *ubbhuta*; in the attainment of self, knowledge is *uppanna*; in capability, one is able to go;
in the statement of form, one *uddisati* the Sutta.

*Abhi* signifies facing toward (*abhimukhabhāva*), excellence (*visiṭṭha*), superiority (*adhika*), high action (*uddhakamma*), family (*kula*), suitability (*sāruppa*), salutation (*vandana*), and the description of a characteristic that has become a pillar (*lakkhaṇi-tthambhūtakkhāna*).
In the case of *vicchā* (distribution) and so forth: in the sense of being face-to-face, *abhimukha*; he approaches (*abhikkamati*); in the sense of distinguished, *abhidhamma*;

in the sense of superior, *abhivasati*; in the sense of ascending to a higher task, *abhiruhati*. In the sense of birth within a family, *abhijāta*; in the sense of being suitable, *abhirūpa*; in the sense of salutation, *abhivādeti*;

[the usage] regarding characteristics (*lakkhaṇa*) and so forth is the same as the preceding. *Paṭi* means: returned (*paṭigata*), contrary (*paṭiloma*), counterpart (*paṭinidhi*), counter-gift (*paṭidāna*), prohibition (*nisedha*), turning back (*nivattana*), similarity (*sādissa*), and giving in exchange for something done (*paṭikaraṇādāna*).

[The prefix] *paṭi-* [is used] in the senses of: awakening (*paṭibodha*), dependence (*paṭicca*), a statement regarding a characteristic that has become fixed (*lakkhaṇitthambhūtakkhāna*), a portion (*bhāga*), and distribution (*vicchā*).

In the sense of "gone toward" (*paṭigata*): *paccakkhaṃ*. In the sense of "opposite" (*paṭiloma*): *paṭisotaṃ*. In the sense of "representative" (*paṭinidhi*): "the pupil stands in for the teacher" (*ācariyato pati sisso*). In the sense of "giving back" (*paṭidāna*):

"he gives back a jar to one who needs oil" (*telatthikassa ghataṃ paṭidadāti*). In the sense of "prohibition" (*nisedha*): *paṭisedheti*. In the sense of "returning" (*nivattana*): *paṭikkamati*. In the sense of "likeness" (*sādisya*): *paṭirūpakaṃ*. In the sense of "remedy" (*paṭikaraṇa*): *paṭikāro*.

In the sense of taking up: *paṭiggaṇhāti* (he receives). In the sense of awakening: *paṭivedho* (penetration). In the sense of depending upon: *paccayo* (condition). Regarding its characteristics (*lakkhaṇa*) and so forth, it is similar to the preceding [prefix *pati-*]. The prefix *pari-* signifies:
