*Bhuja* means "to protect" and "to eat"; with the substitution of *kkha* for *dinā*, one says *bhokkhati* or *bhuñjissati*. *Kusa* means "to revile";
when preceded by the prefix *ā-*, its vowel is shortened, and it should be understood as *ākosati*, etc., involving the suffix *lavikaraṇa*, elision (*lopa*), and vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*).
34. *Kusā* and *ruhehi* [are examples].

*Kusā* and *ruhā* may also occur as substitutes for *issa* and *chi*. Examples include *akkocchi* and *akkosi*, where the first syllables of the following forms (*pararūpa*) have been elided. *Abhi-pubbo ruha* means "in growing"; examples include *abhirucchi* and *abhiruhi*.
*Vaha* means "to reach" (*pāpuṇane*); examples are *vahati* and *vahanti*. In the passive (*kamme*), there is a reversal according to the rule "the elision of *ha*," by which that [form] occurs.
It is carried away; thus it is said, "it is water" (*assū*). It will carry, it will be carried. It carried, it was carried, it carried.
It will carry, it will be carried, and so forth. It may carry, it may be carried. Let it carry, let it be carried, and so forth. *Jara* means aging.
5,174. *Jara* becomes *jīra* before suffixes such as *-mīyaṅ* and *-māna*.
[In the active voice: *jīyati*. With the addition of the augment *īma* and the substitution of *l* for *r* according to the rule "after *jara*, *sadāna*, etc., *īma* is added," it becomes *jīrati*.
In the passive (*kamme*): *jīrīyati*, *jīyīyati*. Likewise: *jīyissati*, *jīrissati*; *jīyīyissati*, *jīrīyissati*.
*Ajīyi*, *ajīri*; *ajīyīyi*, *ajīrīyi*. *Ajīyissā*, *ajīrissā*; *ajīyīyissā*, *ajīrīyissā*, *ajīyissā*, *ajīrīyissā*, and so forth. *Mara* = to give up life (*pāṇacāge*);
with the suffix *īyaṅ*, *mīyati*, *marati*; *mīyanti*, *maranti*, and so forth.
*Disa* = to see (*pekkhane*).
5,124. *Disassa passa, dassa, dasa, da, dakkhāti*: these are the substitutes for *disa* (the optative suffix).

Because it consists of multiple phonemes (*anekavaṇṇattā*), it is a substitute for the whole word. [Examples: *passati*, *passanti*; *dakkhati*, *dakkhanti*. In the passive voice (*kamme-kye*), the original form is preserved: *dissati*, *dissanti*, *vipassīyati*, *dakkhīyati*, and so forth.
6,69. *Dakkha + kha + heti + hohīti lopo*: there is elision (*lopa*) of *kha*, *he*, and *ho*.
With the substitutes *dak* and so forth, there is optionally the elision of the *ss* of another [suffix].
*Dakkhati*, *dakkhissati*. *Apassi*, *passi*; *apassiṃsu*, *passiṃsu*; *apasso*, *passo*; *apassittha*, *passittha*. *Apassiṃ*, *passiṃ*; *apassimha*, *passimha*.
Likewise, *adassī*, *dassī*; *adassiṃsu*, *dassiṃsu*, and so forth. In the non-present tense, there is the substitute *das*. *Addasā*.
*Addasa*: *addā*, *adda*, etc. *Apassissa*, *dakkhissa*, etc. *Passeyya*, *dakkheyya*; *passatu*, *dakkhatu*, etc. *Sada* [is used] in the senses of dispersing, going, censuring, and taking;

preceded by *ni-*, with the augment *īma* according to the rule "after *jaras*, *sadāna*, and *mīma*, there is the augment *īma*": *nisīdati*, *nisīdanti*, etc. In the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*): *nisajjati*, *nisajjate*.
*Yaja* [is used] in the senses of worshipping deities, making an alliance, and giving; *yajati*, *yajanti*, etc. In the passive (*kamme*)—
5,113. Regarding *yajassa yassa ṭi-yī*:
when *ṭi* and *yī* follow *yaj*, by virtue of the rule of frequent usage (*bahulādhikāra*), they occur even in the domain of *tyādi* suffixes;

thus, in the case of *kye*, there is both the prior form (*pubbarūpa*) and the forms *ijjati* and *yijjati*. [Examples: *mayā buddho ijjati*, *yijjati*; *so yajissati*, *tena ijjissate*, *yijjissate*; *so yajī*.

By that, it succeeded (*ijji*), it was successful (*yijji*). He will sacrifice (*yajissā*), by that he will succeed (*ijjissā*), he will be successful (*yijjissā*). He may sacrifice (*yajeyya*), by that he may succeed (*ijjeyya*), he may be successful (*yijjeyya*).
Let him sacrifice (*yajatu*), by that let him succeed (*ijjatu*), let him be successful (*yijjatu*), and so forth.

In *vada* (in the sense of speaking), by the rule "for *gama*, *vada*, etc.," there is optionally the substitution of *vajja* for *vada*; for the *l* sound, by the rule "for *la*, *ū* [occurs] in some cases," there is also *e*, thus *vajjati*.
He speaks (*vadeti*), they speak (*vadanti*); he causes to speak (*vajjeti*), they cause to speak (*vajjenti*), and so forth. In the passive (*kamme*):

it is spoken to (*vadiyyati*), it is spoken (*vadiyyati*), it is spoken to (*vadiyyati*); they are spoken to (*vadiyyanti*), they are spoken (*vadiyyanti*), they are spoken to (*vadiyyanti*). He will speak (*vadissati*), they will speak (*vadissanti*).

He spoke (*avadī*), he spoke (*avadī*); they spoke (*avadiṃsu*), they spoke (*vadiṃsu*). Having spoken (*avadissa*), having spoken (*vadissa*). He should speak (*vajje*), he should speak (*vajjeyya*), he should speak (*vade*), he should speak (*vadeyya*); they should speak (*vajjeyyuṃ*), they should speak (*vadeyyuṃ*). Let him speak (*vajjetu*).
“Vadetu,” “vadatu,” and so forth, should be understood according to the grammatical tradition (*āgama*).
The root *kam* means “to step. By the inclusion of the particle *ca* in the rule “*parokkhāyañcā*,” when there is reduplication as in *kama kama*, the initial consonant is elided;

then, after applying the suffix *la* (the *vikaraṇa*) and changing the *ka* to a guttural according to the rule “*kavaggahā*,” and further applying the insertion of a nasal (*niggahīta*) before the *ca*, one forms *caṅkamati*, *kamati*, and so on.

*Cal* = to shake; *cañcalati*. *Jal* + *dal* = in the sense of shining; *daddallati*, etc. (The system of roots beginning with *bhū*, including the vowel increment). *Hū* + *bhū* = in the sense of existence (*sattā*). In the *ty*-group and others, by the rule “*lo* [is substituted] for the agent,” *lo* is applied.

Upon its elision, by the rule “*e* replaces the semi-vowels *yu* and *vaṇṇa* before a suffix,” the vowel *o* occurs. Thus: *so hoti*, *te honti*; *hosi*, *hotha*; *homi*, *homa*, etc. In the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*): by him it is sacrificed, *hūyati*, *hūyate*. 31. Regarding the substitution of *he*, *hehi*, and *hohi* for *hū* in the future tense (*ssat*), etc.: [the forms become *hesati*, *hehiti*, *hohiti*, etc.]
*Hūssa*, *he*, *ādayo*, *honti*, *ssaccādo*. *Hessati*, *hehi*, *ssati*, *hohissati*.
69. *Dakkha-kha-hehi-hohīhi lopoti*:
There is elision (*lopa*) of the following *ss-* after the substitutes *dakkha*, *kha*, *hehi*, and *hohī*. *Hehiti*, *hehissati*; *hohiti*, *hohissati*.
*Hehinti*, *hehissanti*, *hohinti*, *hohissanti*, and so forth. When the suffix *īm* occurs not in the sense of the present day (*anajjatane*), there is the augment *añ*;

by the rule "the following [vowel] is sometimes elided," the *ī* is dropped, and thus it becomes *so ahu*. In the sense of growth (*vuddhi*), by the rule "a long vowel replaces the *ī* of *īssa*," the substitute *si* is applied to *īssa*, resulting in *suvo ahosi ānando*.
41. *Hūto resuṃ*.

The root *hu* (to sacrifice), when followed by another suffix beginning with *i*, becomes *hū*. The letter *r* is an indicatory (*anubandha*) marker; by the rule “when *r* is an indicatory marker, [the final vowel] of that which begins with a vowel,” there is elision of the final vowel. Thus: *ahesuṃ*. When *a* is substituted for *o*, it becomes *ahavuṃ*. When *si* is substituted for *ossa*, it becomes *ahosi*. 46. *Iṃssa ca siña*:

After the suffix *im*, *siña* is frequently substituted for the endings *mhā* and *atthānaṃ*. The letter *ñ* serves the purpose of indicating the subsequent element (*ākhyāvayavattha*), while the letter *u* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇattha*).
By the rule beginning with “*āissā*,” there is the *i*-augment (*iñāgama*), resulting in *tumhe ahosittha* and *ahosi*.

When the *para-saralopa* (elision of the following vowel) and the shortening (*rasse*) apply, we have *ahuṃ*, *ahosimha*, and *ahumha* (with shortening). In the passive (*bhāve*), [the forms are] *abhavi* and, with the substitution of *āssattha*, *abhavittha*. When the suffixes *āu* etc.

are applied for the non-present tense (*anajjatane*), by the rule “*yuvaṇṇānaṃ iyaṅuvaṅa sare*,” there is the substitution of *uvaṅ*, resulting in *ahuvā*, *ahuvu*, *ahuvo*, and *ahuvattha*. [In the first person singular], *assa* becomes *am*.
*ahuṃ*, *ahuvaṃ*, *ahumha*, and so forth. In the passive (*bhāve*)—*ahuyi*, *ahuyittha*. *Ahavissā*, *ahavissaṃsu*, and so forth. In the passive—*ahuyissa*, *ahuyissatha*.
With the elision of the preceding vowel and the *r*, *heyya*, *heyyuṃ*, and so forth. In the passive—*hūyeyya*, *hūyetha*.
*Hotu*, *hontu*, and so forth. In the passive—*hūyatu*, *hūyataṃ*. With *anu-* as a prefix, *anubhoti*, and so forth, in all sections.
It should be applied. Because there is an absence of *rūpa* (form) in the sense of state (*bhāva*). In the sense of object (*kamma*), there is the distinction such as *anubhūyati*, etc.

Regarding *si* = *saye*: there is elision of *la* and vowel-lengthening (*vuddhi*), resulting in *seti*. With the substitution of *ay*, one has *sayati*, *senti*, *sayanti*, etc. In the sense of object, preceded by *ati*:

when *kye* is applied and the lengthening of the vowel following *i* is performed according to the rule "the long vowel for *sarassa*," one has *atisīyati*, *atisīyanti*, etc. In the sense of state, by that...
*sīyati*, *sīyate*. Likewise in *bhavissati* and so forth. *Nī* means "to lead";

this is a transitive verb (*dvikammaka*)—e.g., *ajaṃ gāmaṃ neti*, *nayati*; *nenti*, *nayanti*, etc. In the passive (*kamme*): *ajo devadattena gāmaṃ nīyate*, etc. The same should be applied to the remaining [roots] as well.
*Ṭhā* means "stopping of motion"—
5,175. Regarding *ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā*:
they become *tiṭṭhapivā* in the case of suffixes such as *n*, *ta*, *māna*, and so on. When *l* is elided, [the forms] are *tiṭṭhati*, *tiṭṭhanti*, *ṭhāti*, and *ṭhānti*.
5,131. According to the rule *pādito ṭhāssa vā ṭhaho kvaci*: in some cases, the *ṭh* of the root *ṭhā* becomes *ṭha* after a prefix.
After *pādi*, there is optionally the substitution of *ṭha* for *ṭhā*. [Examples: *saṇṭhahati*, *saṇṭhahanti*; *lasse*, *adhiṭṭheti*, *adhiṭṭhenti*. In the section on the object (kamma): 5.137.

After *aññādi*, before *kye*, there is the substitution of *ī* for a verbal root (*kriyattha*) ending in *ñ* or another consonant that ends in *ā*. [Examples: *upaṭhīyati*, *upaṭhīyanti*. In the case of the substitute *ṭha*: [the rule applies].

“Kyassā” is the suffix *ī*. By means of it, one is established (*patiṭṭhahīyati*), they are established (*patiṭṭhahīyanti*). With the suffix *īm* expressing the abstract state (*bhāva*), one is established (*ṭhīyati*, *ṭhīyate*).

Likewise, with the prefix *pa-*: he will establish himself (*patiṭṭhissati*, *patiṭṭhahissati*). With the suffix *īssim*: he stood (*aṭṭhāsi*), they stood (*aṭṭhaṃsu*); he stood firmly (*saṇṭhahi*), they stood firmly (*saṇṭhahiṃsu*).

With the suffix *patiṭṭhissa*: he would establish himself (*patiṭṭhahissa*). [In the optative: he might stand (*tiṭṭhe*, *tiṭṭheyya*); he might stand firmly (*saṇṭhe*, *saṇṭheyya*); they might stand firmly (*saṇṭheyyuṃ*).
*Saṇṭhahe*: one should stand firm; *saṇṭhaheyya*. *Tiṭṭhatu*, *ṭhātu*, *saṇṭhahatu*, and so forth. *Pā* = to drink.

With the substitution of *piva*, it becomes *pivati*. By the rule "tavaggavaraṇā" and by the division of the grammatical connection (*yogavibhāga*) "bayañā," the letter *v* is replaced by *b*, thus *pibati*. In the passive, *pīyati*, *pīyanti*, and so forth.
*Asa* = to exist.
52. *Tassa tho*:

For that [word ending in] *at*, there is *tha* for another [suffix]. There is also [the substitution of *tha*] when the first syllable of the subsequent form is *ta*. By the rule “*Nta+māna+nti+yi+yuṃsu ādilopo*,” there is elision of this [initial vowel], resulting in *santi*. 53. *Sihisva ṭa*: After [a word ending in] *si*, there is *ṭa* for *su*.

In this case, *aṭ* occurs for *asi*. *Ṭ* serves the purpose of a universal substitute (*sabbādesattha*). You are (*tvaṃ asi*). When the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) and other changes have been made, now there are "you" (*tumhe attha*). 54.
*Mimānaṃ vā mhimhā ca asasmā paresaṃ:* After *asasmā*, the forms *mimānaṃ* and *mhimhā* optionally occur; by that same rule, *aṭ* also occurs for *asa*. I am (*amhi*).

55. In these [cases], "so" (sa) becomes "esu" and "mimesu" for the purpose of subverting the form of the subsequent word (*pararūpa*). [The forms are: *asmi*, *amha*, *asma*. In the future tense suffix (*bhavissati-paccaya*), [the rule applies] in cases such as *a + ā + ssa* and so forth. (Pāṇini 6.1.94).

In place of *atthi* (the verb "to be"), *bhu* is substituted when it follows a remote past participle (*parokkhā*), a non-recent past participle (*anajjatanā*), a conditional (*kriyātipatti*), or a future tense (*bhavissati*).
This substitution rule is intended to prevent the application of the suffix *-s*. Therefore, forms such as *asitabba* do not occur.
Examples: * Future tense: *bhavissati*, *bhavissanti*. * Remote past: *abhavā*, *abhavu*. * Conditional (*kriyātipatti*): *abhavissa* (with the substitution of *bhu*).
"abhavissaṃsu," and so forth. Regarding the suffixes beginning with *eyya*:
50. *Atthi* + *eyyādi*-suffixes: *sa*, *su*, *sa*, *satha*, *saṃ*, *sāma*.

After the root *as* (in the sense of "to be") followed by suffixes beginning with *eyya*, the substitutes *sa*, *su*, *sa*, *satha*, *saṃ*, and *sāma* occur respectively. By the rule of subsequent form (*pararūpa*), *so* becomes *assa*.
They would be: *te assu*. You would be: *tvaṃ assa*, *tumhe assatha*. I would be: *ahaṃ assaṃ*, *mayaṃ assāma*.

In the case of *tvādi*, *so* becomes *atu*; when *assa* is elided, it becomes *santhu*; with the substitution of *ay*, *tvaṃ* becomes *ahi*; *tumhe* becomes *attha*. In the first person singular, *amhi* and *amha* become *asmi* and *asma* through the substitution of *as*.
Due to the rule of diversity (*bahulādhikārā*), in the present tense (*ajjatana*) forms such as *āsi*, *āsiṃsu*, and *āsuṃ* also occur.
Regarding the rule for the verb *brū* (to speak): 36.
After *brū*, the suffixes *tissī* and *ñā* optionally become *ī* and *īñ*. When the augment (*vuddhi*) has been substituted and the suffix *la* has been elided, [the form] is *bravīti*.
5.97. *Brū* does not become *brūs* before a consonant. It becomes *brūti*. In the substitution of *uva*, it becomes *brūvanti*.
20. For *tya* and *antī*, there is *ṭa* and *ṭū*.

*Āhā paresaṃ ti-antīnaṃ ṭa-ṭū honti.* (After *āha*, for the following *ti* and *anti* endings, *ṭa* and *ṭū* are substituted. The letter *ṭ* serves the purpose of indicating that all [the preceding vowels] are replaced.

For this very reason, the prescription of *ṭa* and *ṭū* after *āha* for the *ti* and *anti* endings indicates that *āho* is substituted for *brū* in the *ti* and *anti* endings. Thus: *āha*, *āhu*; *brūsi*, *brūtha*; *brūmi*, *brūma*, and so forth.
[In the future tense: *bravissati*. [In the aorist: *abravi*, *abruvī*, *abruvuṃ*. In the non-recent past (*anajjatana*), [the forms are] *abravā*, *abruvā*. In the remote past (*parokkhā*):—

16. *Ādīsvāho brūssa*: after the root *brū*, *āho* becomes *brūssa* in the *parokkhā* (aorist) and other tenses. For example: *supine kira so āha* ("it is said that he said in a dream"), *te āhu* ("they said"), and so forth. *Abravissa* ("he spoke"). *Brave* ("may he speak"); *braveyya* ("he might speak"). In the prohibition of *vuddhi* (vowel strengthening), it is *brūtu* ("let him speak"), *bravantu* ("let them speak"), and so forth.

The root *hana* means "to injure. In the third person singular (*timhi*), with the elision of the suffix (*vikaraṇa*), it is *so hanati* or *hanti*. *Te hananti* ("they kill"), and so forth. In the passive voice (*kamme*), there is a prior form (*pubbarūpa*) for *na* [the passive suffix] before *ññe*; thus: *haññati* ("is killed"), *haññanti* ("are killed"), *haññare* ("are killed"). Likewise: *hanissati* ("will kill"), and so forth.

67. *Hanā cha-khā*: For the root *han*, the substitutes *cha* and *kha* occur. Thus: *paṭihaṃkhāmi* (I shall strike back), *paṭihanissāmi* (I will strike back); *haṃchema* (we shall strike), *hanissāma* (we will strike). Forms such as *ahani* (he struck) and *ahanisū* (they struck) should be applied in all instances. Regarding *hu* and so forth: *hu* means "to call. In the *ty-ādi* (present tense) suffixes, the substitution *lo* occurs.
By the inclusion of the word "and" (*ca*) in the rule "In the *parokkhā* [aorist] also," there is doubling (*dvitta*) for *hu* to become *huti*. [The rule continues: "For gutturals (*kavagga*)."

Regarding *cavaggaja*: [from the root] *hu*, there is the elision of *la* and the vowel increment (*vuddhi*). One offers the fire (*aggiṃ juhoti*), except in the case of "the letter *va* after *ya* and a vowel" (*yavā sare*).
[Thus: *juhvati*. *Juhonti*. *Juhvanti*. *Juhoṣi*, *juhvasi*; *juhotha*, *juhvatha*, and so forth. In the passive (*kamme*):
by the rule "the vowel becomes long" (*dīgho sarassā*), the fire is offered by that [means], and so forth. *Juhissati*, *juhissanti*. *Ajuhavi*, *ajuhosi*.
*ajuhaṃsuṃ*, *ajuhaṃviṃsu*, *ajuhaṃsu*, *ajuhosuṃ*. *Ajuhiṃsa*, *ajuhiṃsasu*. *Juhe*, *juheyya*. *Johotu*, *juhontu*, etc. The root *hā* means "to abandon.

As in the previous [conjugation], after the elision of the doubling (*dvebhāva*) and the elision of the *chādesa* suffix, by the rule "the preceding vowel becomes short" (*rasso pubbassā*), the shortening of the preceding *ā* occurs:
*jahāti*, etc. In the passive voice: by the rule "for *kye*, *ā* becomes *ī*" (*aññādissāssī kye*), the *ā* becomes *ī*: *hīyati*, etc. *Jahissati*. *Ajahāsi*.

Regarding the form *dīghā īssa*: [the root] *si* (to abandon) becomes *pajahati*; [its past participles are] *pajahittha*, *ajahiṃsu*, *ajahaṃsu*, *pajahisu*, *pajahuṃ*. In the passive (*kamma*), it is *pahīyi*, *pahīyittha*. It should also be understood in forms beginning with *ssādi*, *eyyādi*, and *tvādī*.

The root *dā* (to give) has two states of being (*dvibhāva-rassatta-nī*). With the elision of *la* (*lalopa*), we have *dadāti*, *dadanti*, and so forth. By the rule "gamavadā" etc., when there is the substitution of *dajja*, we have *dajjati*, *dajjanti*, and so forth. In the case of the suffix *lassa* followed by *kāra*, we have *dānaṃ deti*, and so forth.

22. For the word *dā* (to give), when it occurs with the suffixes *da*, *mim*, or *esu*, there is optionally the substitution of *dam* for *dā*. [Examples: *vaggantaṃ*, *dammi*, *demi*, *damma*, *demā*.

In the case of the vowel *ī*, [we have] *dīyati*, etc. When expressing a future sense (*anāgatattha*), with the augment *iṅ*, [we have] *dassati*, *dassanti*; [and with the conditional suffix] *dajjissati*.
They will give. In the sense of causing to give (*lavikaraṇe*), he will cause to give; they will cause to give. In the present tense (*ajjatane*):
*adadi*, *adadiṃsu*, *adajji*, *adajjiṃsu*, *adāsi*, *adaṃsu*. In the non-present tense (*anajjatane*): *adadā*, *adadu*. In the past tense (*kālātipattiyaṃ*):

*adadissa*, *adajjissa*, *le adassa*, *dassuṃsu*. In the optative (*eyyādimhi*): *dade*, *dadeyya*, *dajje*, *dajjeyya*. By the rule of frequent usage (*bahulādhikārā*), the substitution of *dajja* for *ṭā* occurs in the following form.

*Eyyassa*: *ṭā*, *dajjā*, *dajjuṃ*, *dajjeyyaṃ*, *dadeyyuṃ*. In the *tvādīsu* (second person) group: *dadātu*, *dadantu*, *dajjatu*, *dajjantu*; with the suffix *lassa* followed by *kāra*, *detu*, *dentu*, etc.
In all cases, this should also be applied to the object (*kamma*). *Dhā* = "to hold";

by the inclusion of *tyādi* and the following, when there is reduplication (*dvitta*), the preceding vowel becomes short (*rassatta*), and after the elision of *la* (*lalopa*), [the rule] "of the fourth and second [cases]" applies.
When the letter *da* is substituted for the *da* of *pubbadhakāra*, one forms *dadhāti* and *dadhanti*. With the prefix *pi-* and by the rule beginning with "tadaminā," there is the elision of *ā*;
then, by the rule "dhāssa ho," the letter *ha* replaces the subsequent *dhā* in the reduplicated form, resulting in *pidahati* and *pidahanti*.

With the letter *la* and the suffix *kāra*, one forms *nidheti* and *nidhenti*. In the passive voice, one forms *vidhīyati* and *vidhīyanti*, and so forth. [The future forms are] *dhassati* and *pidahissati*.
*paridahessati*. *adhāsi*, *pidahi*. *adhassa*, *pidahissa*. *dadhe*, *dadheyya*; *pidahe*, *pidaheyya*.
*dadātu*, *pidahatu*, *nidhetu*, *nidhentu*, and so forth. (The *juhotyādi* group).
Both the *bhūvādi* and the *juhotyādi*—these are the *huvādi* verbal roots.
Through the addition of *savuddhika* (*s*) and *bhūvādi*, they undergo a threefold division.
(The *bhūvādi* method.
Now, for the purpose of illustrating the various types of *vikaraṇas*, some forms of the eight classes beginning with *rudh* shall be cited:
*Rudh* (to obstruct) and the others become [the root *ruṇaddhi*, etc.]. Likewise in all subsequent grammatical groups. 5.19.

In the case of *rudh*-type roots (*rudhādi*), when suffixes such as *māna*, *anta*, *ti*, and so forth—which are prescribed for the agent (*kartṛ*) and occur after non-proximate [persons]—are present, *l* replaces the final vowel of *mañ* and the following consonant. [This applies] to the *niggahīta* (anusvāra).

At the end of a *vaga* (labial group), there is no *vṛddhi* strengthening because of the presence of a conjunct (*saṃyoga*), as in *lahussupantassa*. [Examples include: *so maggaṃ rundhati*, *rundhanti*, etc.
With the prefix *ni-* and the root *kyo* (from *rujjhati*), *dha* is replaced by a *ca-vaga* letter, followed by the original form and the third vowel *ja-kāra* (i.e., *i*);
thus: *maggo nirujjhati*, etc. With the augment *iṅ*, we have *rundhissati*, *nirujjhissati*. [Aorist forms: *arundhi*, *arundhiṃsu*. [Precative form: *nirujjhittho*.

It ceased, they ceased. It will cease, they will cease; it would cease, they would cease. It ceases, it may cease; it ceases, it may cease. Let it cease, let them cease. You cease, you cease (imperative). Let it cease, let them cease—thus and so forth. *Chid* means "cutting in two":
*chindati*, *chindanti*. In the passive (*kamma*): *chijjati*, *chijjanti*. In the future tense (*bhavissatipaccaya*)...
— By the rule “*labha vasacchidā*,” etc., for the substitution of *chaṅ*, there are: *checchati*, *chindissati*. In the passive (*kamma*): *pubbarūpaṃ*, *chijjissati*, *chijjissanti*.
Aorist: *achindi*, *chindi*; *acchejji*, *acchejjiṃsu*. Future: *acchindissā*, *achijjissā*. Optative: *chinde*, *chindeyya*;
*chijje*, *chijjeyya*. Imperative: *chindatu*, *chindantu*; *chijjatu*, *chijjantu*, and so forth.
*Bhuja* [is used] in the senses of protecting and consuming; for example, *bhuñjati*, *bhuñjanti*, and so forth.

In the future tense, according to the rule “*bhuja-muca-vaca-visānaṃ kkhaṅa*,” there is a substitution of *kkhaṅ* for *ss* together with the final vowel of the root, resulting in the vowel increment (*vuddhi*): *bhokkhati*, *bhuñjissati*, *bhokkhanti*, *bhuñjissanti*, and so forth.
*Muc* means "releasing": *muccati*, *muccanti*, etc. In the passive (*kamma*), it is *muccati*, *muccanti*, etc. (The *rudh*-class method).
*Div* [is used] in the senses of play, desire to win, trade, splendor, praise, and going: 5.21.
After *div* and the following roots, the suffix *yaka* is applied.

The suffix *yaka* occurs after roots beginning with *div-* when the agent (*kattar*) is expressed and the object (*lavisaya*) is not. The letter *k* serves the purpose of causing the *kānubandha* (the *ka* suffix marker).
This applies here and above as well. When *v* is followed by *b*, there is the *pubbarūpa* (single-substitute) sandhi; thus: *so jutaṃ dibbati*, *dibbanti*, and so forth.
In the passive (*kamme-kye*), it is: *tena dibbati*, *dibbanti*, and so forth. [Future: *dibbissati*, *tena dibbissati*. [Aorist: *adibbi*, *dibbi*; *tena adibbi*, *dibbi*. [Conditional: *adibbissa*.
*Tena adibbissa*: *dibbe*, *dibbeyya*; *tena dibbe*, *dibbeyya*; *dibbatu*; *tena dibbatu*, and so forth.

*Śiv-*, meaning "to sew" (*tantusantāne*): *sibbati*, *sibbanti*, and so forth. *Pad-*, meaning "to go": preceded by the prefix *upa-*; with the substitution of the *ca*-group and the formation of the prior form (*pubbarūpa*):
*uppajjati*, *uppajjare*, *uppajjanti*, and so forth. In the sense of the object (*kamma-kāraka*): *tena paṭipajjate*, and so forth. In the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva-kāraka*): *uppajjate*.
*Tayā* (by that). *Budha* = to understand; among the *yakkhara* vowels, there are the forms with the prefix *jh*. Examples: *dhammaṃ bujjhati*, *bujjhare*, *bujjhanti*, etc.
In the passive (*kamma*), examples: *mayā dhammo bujjhate*, etc. *Yudha* = combat; examples: *yujjhati*, etc. *Naha* = binding;
according to the rule "there is a substitution for *ha*," there is a substitution for *ya*; examples: *sannayhati*, etc. *Mana* = knowledge; there are the forms with the prefix *ñña*.
*Maññati*, etc. *Tusa* means satisfaction (*tuṭṭhi*); in its original form, it is *tussati*, etc. *Sama* means tranquility (*upasama*); it is *sammati*, etc. *Jana* means birth (*janana*);

in the form "janissā," the substitution of *ā* occurs when a suffix with *kā* as its follower is present, due to the rule of abundance (*bahulādhikāra*). Thus: *so jāyati*, *jāyanti*, etc. Regarding the passive:

because one causes [something] to be born, the suffix *ṇi* is applied by the rule "also after the causative agent" (*payojakabyāpāre ṇāpi ca*), and by the rule "elsewhere also" (*aññatrāpi*), the prohibition of *vṛddhi* is applied.

In the *kyamhi* [suffix], when the long vowel is applied according to the rule "the vowel of the root is long," one forms *janīyati*, *janīyanti*, and so forth. From that, *so jāyissati* ("he will be born"), *tena janissati* ("by him it will be born").

*So ajāyi* ("he was born"), *tena ajanīyi* ("by him it was born"). *So ajāyissa* ("he would have been born"), *tena ajanīyissa* ("by him it would have been born"). *So jāye jāyeyya* ("he might be born"), *tena janīyeyya* ("by him it might be born").
*So jāyatu* ("let him be born"), *tena janīyatu* ("let it be born by him"), and so forth. (The *divādinaya* method).
*Tuda* = in the sense of striking, 5.22.

After *tuda* and the following [roots], *ka* occurs when the agent (*kattṛ*) is expressed and the object (*la*) is not intended. *Tudati*, *tudanti*, etc. In the passive (*kamme*): *tudyati*, *tujjati*.
*tudyare*, *tudyanti*, *tujjare*, *tujjanti*, and so forth. Likewise, *tudissati*, *tujjissati*. *Atudi*, *atudiṃsu*, *atujji*.
*Atudissa*, *atujjissa*; *tudeyya*, *tujjeyya*. *Tudatu*, *tudantu*, *tujjatu*, and so forth. *Vis* means "entering"; it is preceded by *pa-*. As in:
*so gāmaṃ pavisati* ("he enters the village"), and so forth. In the passive voice (*kamme*): *pavisīyati*, and so forth. *Pavisissati*.
It will enter (pavisīyissati). It entered (pāvisi); by means of the suffix *īm*, according to the grammatical analysis (*yogavibhāga*) beginning with "bhujamucā," the *kkha* augment is applied.

[Thus: pāvisi, pavisi, pāvekkhi; they entered the earth (pathaviṃ pāvisiṃsu, pavisiṃsu). It was entered (pāvisīyi). It will be entered (pāvisissa, pavisissa). It may be entered (pāvisīyissa). It should enter (pavise, paviseyya);
with the elision of the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇalopa*), it becomes *pavisīyeyya*. Let it enter (pavisatu, pavisīyatu), and so forth. He pushes away (nudati). The root *disa* means "utterance."
It is pointed out, written, satisfied, and so forth. (The *tudādi* class).
*Ji* = to conquer, 5.23.
*Knā* [is substituted] after *jyā*, etc.

The suffix *knā* occurs after roots beginning with *ji* when the agent (*kattṛ*) is the subject and there is no *l* vowel in the scope [of the rule]. There is no *vṛddhi*. He conquers defilements, they conquer;

by him the defilement is conquered, they are conquered. In the *kye* [suffix], the vowel is long. He will conquer, they will conquer. He conquered, he conquered. He was conquered, he was conquered. He will be conquered.
He will have been conquered. He may conquer. Let him conquer, and so forth. *Ci* means "to accumulate" (*caya*); likewise: he accumulates, they accumulate, and so forth.
Ñā, in the sense of understanding (avabodhane), 5,120. Ñāssa ne jā:
for the root ñā, *jā* occurs before the letter *na*. [Thus: vijānāti.
61. Regarding *ñā* and *sanā*:
in the third [case], there is optionally *ñā* for *sanā* and *nā* for *ñā*. Examples include *nāyati*, *vijānāti*, etc. In the passive (kamma), examples include *viññāyati*, etc. Regarding *kye*:
here, by the analysis of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) "and *āsse*," *ā* becomes *e* after *ass*. When *ya* is doubled, it becomes *ñeyyati*, *ñeyyanti*.

And so forth. [In the future tense: *vijānissati*, *vijānissanti*. In the passive (*kamme*): when the *ky* suffix is elided and the doubling (*rass*) is applied to the *ssa*, one forms *ñāssati*, *ñāssanti*, *viññāyissati*, *paññāyissati*.
For in the passive, the *ssa* [is treated thus].

In the case of another person’s *ñāta* [participle], there are optionally the forms *eyyassa*, *iyā*, and *ñā*. Thus: *paññāyihiti*, *paññāyihinti*. In the case of the future (*añāgama*), there are *samajāni*, *saṃjāni*, *saṃjāniṃsu*, and *samajāniṃsu*. In the case of the past passive participle (*kamme*), there are *paññāyi* and *paññāyiṃsu*. [The conditional forms are] *ajānissa* and, in the case of the past passive participle, *aññāyissa*.
63. In the case of another person’s *eyyassa*, there are optionally the forms *iyā* and *ñā*. Thus: *jāniyā*.

62. When *ñā* is substituted [for *jā*], the *jaṃ* of *sanā* optionally becomes *ñā*. Thus: *jaññā*, *jāneyya*, *jāneyyuṃ*. In the passive: *paññāyeyya*, *paññāyeyyuṃ*. *Vijānātu*, *vijānanthu*. In the passive: *viññāyatu*, and so forth. Regarding *mā* = *māne*:
by the rule “*ā ī ssādīnaṃ byañjanassiña*,” through the separation (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule into *iñā*, there is the insertion of *iñ* and the elision of the preceding vowel.
*mināti*, *minanti*. In the passive: *mīyati*, etc. *lū* in the sense of cutting: by the rule "a short vowel is substituted for *kṇā* and *knā*," the root vowel becomes short;
thus, *lunāti*, *lunanti*. In the passive: *lūyati*, etc. *dhu* in the sense of shaking: *dhunāti*, etc. (*Jyā*-class).
*kī* in the sense of weaving mats.
24. With *kyā* and others, there is *kṇā* in the sense of buying (*lavisaye*). By the rule “*kṇāknāsu rasso*,” [the vowel] becomes short: *kiṇāti*, *kiṇanti*, and so forth. In the passive (*kamme*):
*vikkīyati*, *vikkīyanti*. Future: *vikkiṇissati*, *vikkiṇissanti*. Passive future: *vikkīyissati*, *vikkīyissanti*. Aorist: *akiṇi*, *vikkiṇi*.
*vikkīyi* (he sold). *akiṇissa*, *vikkīṇissa* (he would have bought/sold). *vikkīṇe*, *vikkīṇeyya* (he sold/would sell).

*vikkīye*, *vikkīyeyya* (it was sold/would be sold). *vikkīṇātu*, *vikkīṇantu*, *vikkīyatu*, *vikkīyantu* (let him sell/let them sell), and so forth. *Su* = hearing: *suṇāti*, *suṇanti*, and so forth. *Saka* = ability.
5,121. *Sakā* and *pānaṃ* become *kuka* and *ku* respectively before the suffix *ṇe*.
Thus, there are these grammatical derivations: *sakkuṇāti*, *sakkuṇanti*; *sakkunāti*, *sakkunanti*. 53. Or *sse*.
After *sakka*, the particle *kho* optionally becomes *khu* before vowels beginning with *ī*.
Thus: *sakkhissati*, *sakkhissanti*. 58.

After *sakka*, the particle *kho* optionally becomes *kha* before vowels beginning with *ī*. Thus: *asakkhi*, *sakkhi*; *asakkhiṃsu*, *sakkhiṃsu*. *Asakkhissa*, *asakkhissaṃsu*. *Sakkuṇe*, *sakkuṇeyya*. *Sakkuṇātu*, *sakkuṇantu*.
*Pāpuṇane*: with *pa-* as the prefix; according to the rule “*sakā + pānaṃ kuka + kuṇe*,” it forms *kukate*, meaning “he attains success,” as in *pāpuṇāti*, *pāpuṇanti*, etc.
Active voice: *pāpuṇāti*, *pāpuṇanti*. Passive voice: *pāpīyati*, *pāpīyanti*. Future: *pāpuṇissati*, *pāpuṇissanti*. Passive future:
*pāpīyissati*, *pāpīyissanti*. Aorist: *pāpuṇi*, *pāpuṇiṃsu*. Passive aorist: *pāpīyi*, *pāpīyittha*. Conditional: *apāpuṇissa*. Passive conditional: *apāpīyissa*. Optative: *pāpuṇe*.
*pāpuṇeyya*. *kamme-pāpīyeyya*. *pāpuṇātu*, *pāpuṇantu*. *kamme-pāpīyatu*, etc. (The Kyādi class).
*su* = hearing; 25.
After *svādi* [roots], *kṇa* [is added].

The suffix *kṇa* occurs after roots beginning with *su* in the sense of hearing. Because it has *kā* as its indicatory letter (*anubandha*), there is no *vṛddhi* strengthening. *Dhammaṃ suṇoti* (he hears the Dhamma). When the mutual elision (*paraspara-lopa*) of the suffixes occurs, it becomes *suṇonti*.
In the passive (*kamme-kye*), with lengthening, it is *sūyati*, *sūyanti*. In the reduplicated form (*dvitte*), it is *suyyati*, *suyyanti*, and so forth.

With the insertion of *iṅ* (*iñāgama*), it is *suṇissati*, *suṇissanti*. In the passive, with the elision of *ky* and *la*, there is *vṛddhi*: *sossati*, *sossanti*, and so forth. In the aorist: *asuṇi*, *suṇi*; *asuṇiṃsu*, *suṇiṃsu*.
60. *Suto* becomes *kṇo* or *kṇā* before *ro* and *ṭ*.

Among those [prefixes] beginning with *ī*, *suto* becomes *kṇo* or *kṇā* before the following *ro* or *ṭ*. The letter *r* is an *anubandha*. *Ṭ* serves the purpose of indicating a complete replacement (*sabbādesa*).
When *ussa* is elided, there is doubling (*dvitta*) of *ī* and *si*. [Thus: *assosi*, *assosiṃsu*. By the analysis of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) "and for *ī* and *si*, *ña*," there is *siña*.
*Assosiṃsu*, *paccassosuṃ*. *Asuyi*, *asuyittha*. *Asuṇissa*, *tena asuyissa*. *Suṇe*, *suṇeyya*, *suṇeyyaṃ*.
*Tena sūye*, *sūyeyya*. *Suṇātu*, *suṇantu*. *Sūyatu*, *sūyantu*, etc. *Gi* = sound: *giṇoti*, *giṇanti*. *Tvaṃ giṇosi*. *Giṇissati*, *giṇissanti*.
*Agiṇissa*. *Giṇeyya*. *Giṇotu*, etc. *Vu* = covering: *āvuṇoti*, *āvuṇanti*. *Āvuṇosi*, etc. This should be applied to the remaining [roots] as well. (The method for *svādi*).
Regarding the expansion [of the rules]: 26. *Tanādito*:

After roots beginning with *tan*, the suffix *o* is substituted for *a* when the agent (*kattar*) is expressed and the object (*lavisaya*) is present. Examples include *kittiṃ tanoti* (he spreads fame) and *tanonti* (they spread).

76. Regarding the substitution *o* (*ovikaraṇa*), the substitute *u* occurs in the domain of the subsequent group of six [personal endings]. [Examples: *tanute*, *tanvante*; *tanuse*, *tanuvhe*; *tanve*, *tanvamhe*. In the passive (*kamme*)—according to rule 5.138—the substitute *sā* optionally replaces *tan*.
From the root *tan*, there is the form *ā* with the suffix *kye*. Preceded by *pa*, it becomes *patāyati*. Thus: *pataññati*, *patāyare*, *patāyanti*, *pataññare*, *pataññanti*, and so forth.
Likewise, when the *vikaraṇa* suffix is elided and the augment *i* is inserted, there are:
*tanissati*, *tanissanti*; *patāyissati*; *atani*, *ataniṃsu*; *atanissa*; *patāyissa*; *taneyya*, *taneyyuṃ*; *tanotu*, *tanontu*, and so forth.
*Kara* = *karaṇe*, 5,177.

For the *sa* of *kara*, there are optionally *kubba*, *kuru*, and *kayirā* when the *okāra* (*o*) follows, in the case of suffixes such as *nta*, *māna*, and *ty*. [Examples: *kubbati*, *kubbanti*; *karoti*, *karonti*; *karosi*, *karotha*.
23. Before the suffixes *mim*, the *kuṃ* of *karassa* (the genitive of *kara*) or the *kuṃ* of *okārassa* (the genitive of *o*) becomes *kum*. Examples: *kummi* (*karomi*), *kumma* (*karoma*).
In the following section: *kurute*, *kubbate*, *kubbante*, etc.; *kayirati*, *kayiranti*, etc. In the passive (*kamme*), when the suffix *ky* is doubled, the vowel *ī* becomes short.

[The forms] *kariyyati* or *karīyati*, etc., [are derived from the root *kṛ*]. According to the rule beginning with *tavaggavaraṇā*, when there is a short *y*-sound (*yakāra*), [the suffixes] become *kayyati* and *kayyanti*.

Due to the frequentative nature of the grammatical rules (*bahulādhikārā*), in certain instances of the object case (*kamma*), by means of this substitution of *kayira*, one has *kayirati*, *kayiranti*, etc. In the future tense (*bhavissatimhi*): 25. *Hāssa cā+haṅa ssena* [The substitute] *ha* [is applied] for the vowel *a* [of the suffix], and *haṅa* [is applied] by means of the suffix *ssa*.

In the case of *kā*, *sā*, and *hā*, the augment *āhaṅ* occurs together with the suffix *ssena*. Thus: *kāhati*, *kāhanti*, and so forth. With the insertion of the augment *ī*, it becomes *kāhiti*, *kāhinti*, and so forth. In the alternative where the substitution of *āhaṅ* does not occur, it is *karissati*, *karissanti*, and so forth.
Regarding the present day (*ajjatana*): Rule 24 states that in the case of *kā* and other roots, the vowel *o* of *kā* optionally becomes *kā* before suffixes beginning with *ī*.

44. *Dīghā īssa*: For the long vowel *ī* of the root *kar*, there is optionally the substitution of *ī*. Thus: *akāsi*. When *ī* is elided (*īlope*), it becomes *akā*; *akaṃsu*. When *ī* is replaced by *o*, it becomes *akāsi*.
When *si* is augmented (*siñāgame*), it becomes *akāsittha*. [Other forms are: *akāsi*, *akāsiṃ*, *akāsimha*. Elsewhere: *akarikari*, *akariṃsu*, *kariṃsu*, *akaṃsu*, and so forth.
*Tena akarīyi* and so forth. *Akarissa* and so forth. In the passive voice, *akarīyissa* and so forth.

In the case of the *eyya*-suffixes, when the augment (*ovikaraṇa*) is dropped according to the rule "in some cases the verbal suffixes [are elided]," we have *karekareyya*, *kareyyuṃ*, and so forth. *Kubbe*, *kubbeyya*, and so forth.
There is elision of *eyya* after *parassa* and *kayirā*.
He would do (*so kayirā*). 70. Regarding *kayire*, *yyasse*, *yyum*, and so forth:
there is elision of *eyya* after *parassa* and *eyyum* etc. They would do (*kayiruṃ*). You would do (*tvaṃ kayirāsi*, *kayirātha*). I would do (*kayirāmi*, *kayirāma*).
72. In the case of *ethassā*, *parasse*, *thassa*, *ā*, and so forth, the vowel *ā* occurs in place of *e*. Examples include: *kayirātha dhīro*;
*kamme-kariyeyya*, *kariyeyyu*, and so on; *karotu*, *kurutu*, *kubbantu*, *karontu*, and so on; and in the second person plural, *kurutaṃ*.
*kubbantaṃ* (present participle). *kurussu*, *karassu*, etc. [In these cases] the vowel *a* is substituted by the rule "for *eona*" (*ena*). *kuruvho*, *kubbe*, *kubbāmase*.
In the passive voice: *karīyatu*, etc. 5,133.
Of the root *karoti*...
In the place of *pādi*, *kha* occurs optionally before a following consonant (*kara*). Thus, one should apply this in all instances such as *abhisaṅkharoti*.

In the case of the substitution of *kha* by means of the rule beginning with “*tadaminā*,” the specific form is *abhisaṃkhāsī*. *Saka* [is used] in the sense of power (*satti*); thus, *sakkoti* and so forth. *Apa* [is used] in the sense of reaching (*pāpuṇana*);
preceded by *pa*, it forms *pappoti* and so forth. (This is the method of *tanādi*).
Cura=theyye, 1,15.

After roots beginning with *cur* used in the sense of "to do" (*kriya*), the suffix *ṇi* is added in the sense of the root itself (*sakatthe*). By the rule “*Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā*,” there is optionally *lo*. *Dhanaṃ*...
*Corayati*, *coreti*, and so forth. In the passive (*kamma*), *corīyati*, and so forth. *Corayissati*, *coressati*, and so forth. In the passive, *corīyissati*, and so forth.
*Acorayi*, *corayi*, *acoresi*, *coresi*, and so forth. *Acorayissa*, and so forth. In the passive, *acorīyissa*, and so forth.
*Coraye*, *corayeyya*, and so forth. *Coretu*, *corentu*, and so forth.

*Ciṇṭ* = *ciṇṭāyaṃ* (in the sense of thinking); due to its being a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*), there is no vowel lengthening. One thinks: *ciṇṭeti*, *ciṇṭayati*; they think: *ciṇṭenti*. In the passive voice:
*ciṇṭīyati*, *ciṇṭīyanti*, and so forth. *Mant* = *guttabhāsane* (in the sense of speaking cautiously); one speaks cautiously: *manteti*, *mantayati*, and so forth.
*Pāl* = *rakkhaṇe* (in the sense of protecting); he protects the Dhamma: *pāleti*, *pālayati*. By him it is protected: *pālīyati*, and so forth. (The *curādiniyā* method).
The *bhū-ādi* and *rudh-ādi* groups, the *div-ādi* and *tud-ādi* groups;
the *jyā-ādi*, *kriy-ādi*, and *svā-ādi* groups, as well as the *tan-ādi* and *cur-ādi* groups.
(The Rules for the Application of Vikaraṇas)
5.1. Regarding the suffixes *kha* and *sa*: they occur after the roots *māna*, *khama*, and *vīmaṃsā*.

In the case of *khanti*, the suffix *tijā* occurs; and in the case of *vīmaṃsā*, the suffixes *māna* and *kha* occur, with *sa* as well, respectively. *Tija* means "to sharpen"; there is the elision (*apayoga*) of the vowel *a*.

In the case of *kha*, by the rule "of a light root ending in a vowel," the substitution of *e* for *o* would apply, but this is prohibited by the rule "except elsewhere" (*aññatrāpi*). [This applies] to a consonant other than the letter *y*.

Regarding the rule *“pararūpa mayakāre byañjane”* (the single substitute occurs before a consonant ending in *y* or *k*): there is the *pararūpa* [substitution]. Then, by the rule *“catutthadutiyā”* etc., the first letter *k* is replaced;
and by the rule *“khachasānaṃ ekassaro di dve”* (for *kh*, *ch*, and *s*, a single vowel is substituted and the following consonant is doubled), *tikkha* becomes *tikkha* through doubling;

and when the initial consonant is dropped according to the rule *“lopo nādibyañjanassā”* (elision of the initial consonant), the suffixes *ty-ādi* and the *la-vikaraṇa* are applied to the root *titikkh*. Thus: *titikkhati*, and so forth.
*Purimasamaṃ*. Regarding *kamma*: it is declined as *kamme*, *titikkhīyati*, and so forth. From this point on, we shall not provide further examples of *kamma*.

*Māna*: from the root *mā* (in the sense of honoring) with the suffix *ti*, and after applying the rules for doubling (*dvitta*) and so on, there occurs the substitution of *vī* for the preceding *māna* and *maṃ* for the following *māna*, resulting in *mānavī*.
From the root *vi-maṃsa*, after applying the suffix *ti* and so forth, one forms *vīmaṃsati*, and so on.

"He will endure" (*titikkhissati*), "he will investigate" (*vīmaṃsissati*), and so forth. In this same way, it should also be applied to "today" (*ajjatana*) and other such terms. Because it is the instigator (*payojaka*), the suffix *ṇi* is used;

by the rule "after *ṇi*, *ṇāpi*, and *āpi*, [the suffix] *la* may optionally be elided," the *la*-augment is elided, resulting in *tejayati* and *tejeti*. Likewise, because it belongs to the *curādi* group, the *la*-augment is not elided, resulting in *mānayati* and *māneti*.
5,2. After the root *kit*, the suffix *cha* is used in the senses of healing and doubt.
The suffix *cha* is applied to the root *kit* when it occurs in the sense of healing (*tikicchā*) or doubt (*saṃsaya*).

Since *kit* means "dwelling" (*nivāse*), when the suffix *cha* is added and the rules for prior form (*pararūpa*) and so forth have been applied, there is the doubling according to the rule "of *kit* in the sense of doubt or [healing]," whereby the initial *ti* is substituted for the preceding [vowel] from the root *tikicch*. Thus:

*tikicchati*, *tikicchanti*, etc. When preceded by the prefix *vi-*, after the suffix *cha* and so forth have been added, [the rule] "for gutturals (*kavagga*), there are palatals (*cavagga*)" applies.

In the second [chapter], regarding the roots *kass* and *co*: *vicikicchati*, *vicikicchanti*, etc. Because they are instigators (*payojaka*), *ketayati*, etc., are similar to the preceding [roots]. 5.3. Regarding censure (*nindā*), for *gup* and *badh*, *cha* and *bha* [are substituted] for *va* and *ssa*.

In the context of censure, for the roots *gup* (in the sense of protecting) and *badh*, *cha* becomes [the substitute] for *va* and *ssa*, and *bha* [becomes the substitute] for *va* and *ssa*. From *gup* in the sense of protecting, with the suffix *tīma* and the suffix *cha* according to the rule "elsewhere also" (*aññatrāpi*).

And when there is the absence of *ottā*, and after the substitution of *ja* for *ga* by the rule "kavaggahā" (*kavarga-ha*), the doubling of the preceding syllable occurs by the rule "gupissussā," whereby *ussa* becomes *i*.
Thus, with the addition of suffixes such as *tyādi* and *lavikaraṇādi*, we have forms such as *jigucchati*.

In the sense of censure—derived from *badha* (meaning "binding") with the suffix *tīma* and the *cha*-suffix—the same rule applies, whereby *ba* becomes *bha*, and after the substitution of the single form (*pararūpa*) in the first syllable, we have *bhacchabhacchaiti*.
When there is elision of the initial consonant in a reduplication (dvitta), by the rule "the fourth and second become the third and first," the preceding *bha* becomes *ba*;

then, by the rule "in the presence of *kha*, *cha*, and the remainder, [the vowel] *i* is long," the long *ī* is applied. Thus, from the root *bībhaccha*, the forms beginning with the third person plural (*ty-ādayo*) arise:
*bībhacchati*, *bībhacchanti*, and so forth. In other cases, it is *gopeti*, etc.
5.4. *Tuṃsmā lopo ci+cchāyaṃ te*:

After a word ending in the suffix *tuṃ*, when the sense of desire (*icchā*) is intended, the suffixes *kha*, *sa*, and *cha* occur frequently (*bahulaṃ*), and there is also the elision (*lopa*) of the suffix *tuṃ*.

This is because it has been so heard [in the tradition]. *Bhuja* means "to protect" and "to eat. In the analysis (*viggaha*) of *bhojanāya* (for eating), the suffix *tuṃ* is applied according to the rule beginning with "*tuṃ tāye*" and so forth.
Regarding the phrase “lahussupantassā”: when the *pararūpa* (substitution) of the vowel *o* has been applied, one analyzes it as *bhottum icchati*.

Then, by means of this [rule], the *tuṃ*-suffix is elided by the *kha*-suffix; and according to the principle that “in the absence of the cause, there is also the absence of the effect,” the *pararūpa* and the vowel *o* disappear.
When the *kha*-suffix is applied, followed by the *pararūpa* of *kha*, and so forth, the doubling (*dvitta*) occurs as *bhukkha bhukkha*, wherein the third letter is the vowel *a*.
[The forms] *hoti*, *bubhukkhadhātuto*, and so forth, occur; [from the root] *bubhukkha-* [we get] *bubhukkhati*, *bubhukkhanti*, etc. Regarding *ji* = *jaye* (to conquer):
having analyzed it as *jayanāya* (for the sake of conquering), and having applied the suffixes *tum* and so forth as before, one analyzes *jetum icchati* (desires to conquer).

When the suffix is present, there is reduplication (*dvitta*) of *jisa* and *jisa*; with the elision of the non-initial consonant (*anādibyañjanalopa*) and the reduplication, for the subsequent *jissa*, [the form] *jiharānaṃ* [is derived].
*Giṃ* means *giṃ*. From the root *jigiṃsa*, in forms such as *jigiṃsati* and *jigiṃsanti*, and so forth. From the root *ghasa* (to eat):

in *ghasituṃ micchati*, when the suffix *cha* and others are applied as before, the *gha* becomes *jha* by the rule "from gutturals" (*kavaggahā*), the *jh* becomes *ja* by the rule "the fourth and second [consonants]" (*catutthadutiyā*), and the vowel *i* is substituted by the rule "in place of *a* when *kha*, *cha*, and *śa* follow" (*khachasesvassī*). Thus, from the root *jighaccha*:
[The forms] *tyādayo* and so forth occur. *Jighacchati*, *jighacchanti*, and so on. 5.5. *Īyo kammā*:

The suffix *īya* occurs after a verb expressing desire (*icchākamma*) in the sense of desiring. Because the suffix *īya* is stated [in the rule] beginning with *īyādivuttittā*, there is elision of the case ending due to "identity of meaning" (*ekatthatāyaṃ*). Thus: *puttaṃ icchati* becomes *puttīyati*, *puttīyanti*, and so forth.

5,6. In the sense of acting like something, the suffix *īya* occurs after a noun denoting the object of comparison, in the sense of behaving like that [object]. For example: *puttam ivācarati* (he behaves as if toward a son) becomes *puttīyati sissam* (he behaves toward the pupil as toward a son); likewise, *puttīyanti*, etc. 5,7.
In the sense of a locus (*ādhāra*).

The suffix *āya* occurs [in these senses]. From the root *kuṭ*, as in *kuṭīyati* (he behaves like a hut) in the sense of a palace (*pāsāda*). From the root *pās*, as in *pāsādīyati* (he behaves like a palace) in the sense of a hut (*kuṭī*);
likewise, *pāsādīyanti* and so forth. 5.8.

The suffix *āya* occurs after a noun used as a standard of comparison (*upamāna*) in the sense of behaving like that. For example: "He behaves like a mountain through his possession of qualities such as virtue" is expressed as *pabbatāyati* (he acts like a mountain), referring to a yogi; likewise, *pabbatāyati* from the verbal root *pabbatāya*, and so on.

5,9. In the sense of becoming what one was not (*abhūtatadbhāva*), the suffix *āya* is frequently applied after a word ending in *cyattha*. For example, from a word in the nominative singular (*paṭhamanta*), as in "it becomes intense (*bhusa*) from being non-intense (*abhusa*)," we have *bhusāyati*;

likewise, *bhusāyanti*, and so forth. Regarding the rule "two [words] in the sense of frequency (*ābhikkhaṇṇa*) and repetition (*vicchā*"), when there is reduplication (*dvitta*) in the sense of frequency, we have *apaṭapaṭā*.
"It crackles" (*paṭapaṭā bhavati*) becomes *paṭapaṭāyati*; likewise *paṭapaṭāyanti*, and so forth. "That which was not red becomes red" is *lohitāyati*.
5,10. Regarding the sense "he makes sounds, etc.":

the suffix *-āya-* occurs when the meaning is "he makes [something] with sounds, etc. ending in the accusative case. He makes a sound: *saddāyati*. Similarly, *verāyati* (he bears enmity), *kalahāyati* (he quarrels), *dhūpāyati* (it smokes), and so forth.

5,11. *Namo* becomes *assa* in the sense of "he makes *namo*. In the sense of "he makes *namo*," the suffixes *tya*, etc., occur after the suffix *assa*; for example: *tathāgataṃ namassati*, *namassanti*, and so forth. 5,12.
[The suffix *assa* occurs] after a noun (*nāma*) in the sense of a verbal root (*dhātu*).

The suffix *ami* frequently occurs after a noun in the sense of a verbal root. For example, from *hatthinā atikkamati* ("he passes by with an elephant"), when the suffix *i* is added, and the elision (*luk*) of the *va*-affix and the substitution of *e* for *i* and *ay* for *a* have been applied, it becomes *atihatthayati*.
Similarly: *vīṇāya upagāyati* becomes *upavīṇāyati*; *vinayaṃ daḷhaṃ karoti* becomes *daḷhayati*;
*visuddhā hoti ratti* becomes *visuddhāyati*; *kusalaṃ pucchati* becomes *kusalāyati*, and so forth.

5.13. *Āpi* also occurs after roots such as *sacca* (to speak) when applied to the meaning of a verbal root. In the case of *saccaṃ ācikkhati*, when the suffixes *ty-ādi* follow the suffix *āpi*, the substitution of *e* for the *i* of the *ṇi* suffix occurs by the rule "optionally after *ṇi*, *ṇāpi*, and *āpi*" (*ṇi-ṇāpyā-dīhi vā*).
Thus: *saccāpayati*, *saccāpeti*, and so forth. Similarly, *atthaṃ ācikkhati* becomes *atthāpayati*.
In this way, one causes [something] to be known (*vedāpayati*). "He makes dry" means *sukkhaṃ karoti*, which becomes *sukkāpayati* or *sukkāpeti*, and so forth.
5,16. Regarding the activity of the instigator (*payojaka-byāpāre*):
the suffixes *ṇi* and *ṇāpi* frequently occur after verbal roots (*kriyattha*) in the sense of the activity of one who instigates the agent (*yo payojeti tassa byāpāre*).
The suffix *ṇi* follows verbal roots ending in *u*-vowels (*uvaṇṇa*), while for those ending in *ā*, it becomes *ṇāp*.
For the remaining [roots], two [suffixes] become one optionally;
this is due to the frequent recurrence of the rule "generally" (*bahulaṃ*). Even intransitive roots become transitive when ending in *ṇi* or *ṇāp*.
Transitive roots have two objects, and those with two objects may also have three.
Therefore, the occurrence of the suffixes *ṇi*, *ṇā*, *pi*, and *ina* takes place in relation to both the agent (*kattar*) and the object (*kamma*);
however, it does not occur in the impersonal sense (*bhāve*), nor when there is only a simple agent, nor when the object belongs to the instigator (*payojaka*).
The roots beginning with *padhā* (to strive) take the primary (*padhāna*) suffixes, while those beginning with *duh* (to milk) take the secondary (*apadhāna*).
When the agent is pure (*suddhakattā*), the suffixes *ṇi*, *ṇā*, and *pī* have as their domain the expression of the object (*kamma*) and the past participle (*makkhyāta*).

In the sense of "he causes to become" (*bhavituṃ payojayati*), the suffix *ṇi* is applied by this rule. The letter *ṇ* is an *anubandha* for the purpose of causing the substitution of *e* for the semi-vowels and *u*-vowels (*yuvaṇṇānaṃ e-o*).

In the case of the suffix *paccaya*, by the rule "āyā vā ṇānubandhe" (Pāṇini 6.1.78), there is the substitution of *ā* when followed by a suffix with *ṇ* as its *anubandha*. In the context of the *tyādi* suffixes, by the rule "ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā" (Kaccāyana 3.2.40), there is the substitution of *e* for the *la*-vikaraṇa;
then, by the rule "eona mayavā sare" (Kaccāyana 3.2.41), there is the substitution of *aya*. Thus, one forms "bhāvayati," "bhāveti," "bhāvayanti," "bhāventi," and so forth.
In the passive (*kamma*), it becomes "samādhi bhāvīyati," and so on. Here, [the rule] "dīgho sarassā" (Kaccāyana 3.2.42) applies.
*kye*: the long vowel replaces *i*. Examples include: *bhāvayissati*, *bhāvessati*; *bhāvayissanti*, *bhāvessanti*, and so forth.
In the present tense (*ajjatane*), after the suffix *ī*, in the first person singular (*simhi*), [the forms are]: *abhāvesi*, *bhāvesi*; *abhāvayi*, *bhāvayi*; *abhāvayiṃsu*, *bhāvayiṃsu*.

When there is elision of the following consonant (*parassaralope*), [the forms are]: *abhāvesuṃ*, *bhāvesuṃ*; *abhāvayaṃsu*, *bhāvayaṃsu*; *abhāvayuṃ*, *bhāvayuṃ*, and so forth. In the passive voice (*kamme*): *abhāvīyi*.
*Bhāvīyi*, etc. In the passive: *abhāvissa*, *abhāvayissa*; *abhāvissaṃsu*, *abhāvayissaṃsu*. In the object-voice (passive):
*abhāvayissaṃ*, etc. In the impersonal (bhāve): *bhāveyya*, etc. In the object-voice: *bhāvīyeyya*, etc. In the imperative: *bhāvayatu*, *bhāvetu*, etc.
In the object-voice: *bhāvīyatu*, etc.
In the sense of "he causes to cook," the suffixes *ṇi* and *ṇāpi* are applied. Thus: *so devadattena odanaṃ pācayati*, *pāceti*, and so forth;
likewise, *pācāpayati*, *pācāpeti*, and so forth. In the passive voice: *tena devadattena odano pācīyati*, *pācāpīyati*, and so forth.
This should also be applied to the future tense and other such forms.

Regarding the sense "he employs [someone] to go": *so taṃ purisaṃ gāmaṃ gamayati*, *gameti*, *gacchāpayati*, *gacchāpeti*, etc. In the passive (kamma): *tena so gāmaṃ gamīyati*, *gacchāpīyati*, etc. *Guha* means "concealment" (*saṃvaraṇe*). Regarding "he employs [someone] to conceal":

by the addition of the suffix *ṇi*, there is lengthening according to the rule *“guhissa sare”* (lengthening of the vowel of *guhi* before a vowel). Thus: *gūhayati*, *gūhayanti*, etc. *Disa* and *dusa* mean "displeasure" (*appītiyaṃ*). Regarding "he employs [someone] to feel displeasure":
by the addition of the suffix *ṇi*, there is lengthening according to the rule *“ṇimhi dīgho dusassā”* (lengthening of the vowel of *dusa* when *ṇi* follows). Thus: *dūsayati*, etc.

Likewise, one causes someone who desires to act: *icchāpayati*, *icchāpeti*; one searches: *esayati*, *eseti*. One causes someone who is determining to act: *niyamayati*, *niyameti*. Likewise, one causes to sit:
*āsayati*, *āseti*; one causes to cause to sit: *acchāpayati*, *acchāpeti*. One causes to obtain: *lābhayati*, *lābheti*;
similarly, one causes to dwell: *vāsayati*, *vāseti*, *vāsāpayati*, *vāsāpeti*. One causes to carry: *vāhayati*, *vāheti*, *vāhāpayati*, *vāhāpeti*, and so forth.
Thus: *jīrayati*, *mārayati*, *dassayati*, and so forth. The root *hū* means "existence" (*sattā*); with the causative suffix *ṇi*:

*pahontaṃ payojayati* becomes *pahāvayati*, *pahāveti*, and so forth. [Similarly: *sāyayati*, *sāyāpayati*, *sāyāpeti*; *nāyāpayati*, *nāyāpeti*; *patiṭṭhāpayati*, *patiṭṭhāpeti*. In the short vowel form: *patiṭṭhapeti*.
[The form] *hantuṃ payojayati* (causes to kill) takes the suffixes *ṇi* and *ṇāpi*; according to the rule: “*han* becomes *ghāta* when followed by a suffix beginning with *ṇa*.”
In the *ghātādi* group: *ghātayati*, *ghāteti*. Likewise, *juhāvayati*, *juhāveti*; *jahāpayati*, *jahāpeti*;
*hāpayati*, *hāpeti*; *dāpayati*, *dāpeti*; *vidhāpayati*, *vidhāpeti*; *pidahāpayati*, *pidahāpeti*.
(This is the method for the *bhūvādi* class. Now, the eight classes beginning with *rudh* are shown: *rodhayati*, *rodheti*; *devayati*, *deveti*; *todayati*, *todeti*.
*Jayāpayati*, *jayāpeti*; *vikkayati*, *vikkayāpeti*; *sāvayati*, *sāveti*; *vitānayati*, *vitāneti*;
*corāpayati*, *corāpeti*, and so forth.
With the suffixes beginning with *khādī*, there also occur the causative suffixes *ṇi* and *ṇāpayo*.
The suffixes *ṇi*, *ṇāpi*, *na*, *kā*, and *nā* [are applied here], and in this context, the "seeing" (*dassana*) is the instrument (*sādhana*).
One causes one who is enduring to endure: *titikkheti*, *titikkhāpeti*. One treats medically: *tikicchayati*, *tikiccheti*, *tikicchāpayati*, *tikicchāpeti*.
Likewise, one causes hunger: *bubhukkheti*, *bubhukkhāpeti*. One causes to be like a mountain: *pabbatāyayati*. One acts like a son: *puttīyayati*, and so forth. (The Method of the *khādi* Suffixes).
Thus ends the sixth chapter, beginning with *ty*, in the *Payogasiddhi*.
7. The Chapter on *kha* and Others.

Now, the rules for the suffixes beginning with *kha* are commenced, together with the means of accomplishment such as state (*bhāva*), object (*karman*), agent (*kartṛ*), and instrument (*karaṇa*), derived from verbal roots (*dhātu*) alone.

The formation of the suffixes in *tijamānehi*, *khasā*, *khamāvī*, *mānsāsu*, and so forth, as well as the grammatical operations such as *pararūpa* (substitution of the following form) and *dvitta* (doubling), should be understood according to the method explained in the *Tyādi-kaṇḍa*. *Titikkhā* is the act of enduring;
by the rule “*itthiya + maṇaktikayakayā ca*,” there is the suffix *ap* and also the suffix *āp* [forming] *matvā* for the feminine. Likewise, *vīmaṃsanaṃ*...

*Vīmaṃsā*. Regarding the words *kitā*, *tikicchā*, and *saṃsayesu*: when the suffix *cha* is applied according to the rule beginning with "after six [roots]," we have *tikicchanaṃ* = *tikicchā* (healing), and *vicikicchanaṃ* = *vicikicchā* (doubt).

From the roots *gup* (to protect) and *badh* (to bind), by the rule "for censure, after *gup* and *badh*, the suffix *cha* is added, and the *ba* becomes *bha*," the suffix *cha* is applied, and the subsequent letter *ba* is changed to *bha* by this rule.
[The resulting forms are *gopā* and *bandhā*]. The suffixes beginning with *ap* follow.
There is [the following]: *jigucchanaṃ* is *jigucchā*; *bībhacchanaṃ* is *bībhacchā*.

According to the rule *“tuṃsmā lopo ci+cchāyaṃ te”* (there is elision of *tuṃ* and *smā* before the suffixes *ci*, *cha*, and *kha* when expressing the sense of desire), the suffixes *kha*, *sa*, and *cha* occur in the sense of desire (*icchā*). From the root *bhuja*—meaning "to protect" and "to eat"—comes *bubhukkhanaṃ*, which is *bubhukkhā*.
From *ji*—meaning "to conquer"—comes *jigiṃsanaṃ*, which is *jigiṃsā*. From *ghasa*—meaning "to eat"—comes *jighacchanaṃ*, which is *jighacchā*.
27. Regarding the suffixes *tabba* and *anīya*:

The suffixes *tabba* and *anīya*, when used in the sense of action (*bhāva*) or object (*kamma*), follow verbal roots (*kriyattha*). Due to their extensive application, they also occur after [roots] expressing the agent (*kartṛ*) or the instrument (*karaṇa*), etc.

In the case of the root *bhū* (in the sense of existence): by the rule "for semi-vowels (*yuvaṇṇa*), there is *o* before a suffix," the vowel *o* is substituted; then, by the rule "there is the augment *ū* for a consonant (*ūbyañjanassa*"), the augment *ū* is inserted; the letter *ñ* serves as the initial constituent element.

In the word *bhūyatā*, there is the substitution of *ava* for *eona* (i.e., *bhavana* becomes *bhūyatā*). It is that which must come into being (*bhavitabba*), that which is to be (*bhavatā*), and that which is fit to be (*bhavanīya*).
The state (*bhāva*) is expressed in the singular number alone, and it is of the neuter gender. This state is expressed by the suffixes beginning with *-tabba*.
"Dabbam iva pakāsati" is also plural.
With the prefix "abhi," it refers to the object: anger is to be overcome by the wise—*abhibhūyate*, *abhibhūyittha*, *abhibhūyissate*;
craving is to be overcome; suffering is to be overcome. Thus, [they] are to be overcome, [they] are to be overcome.
The gender and number [of the suffixes] follow those of the object (*abhibhavanīya*) and the action (*kamma*), which is the very thing to be expressed.
[The suffixes] *visesa*, *liṅga*, *itabbādi* (those beginning with *-itabba*), and so on—five such types of abstract nouns (*bhāvajā*)—occur there.
In the neuter gender, they may express the abstract state (*bhāva*), as well as the past participle (*kta*) and the suffix *-ana* used in the non-agentive sense (*akattari*).
In the masculine gender, the word *bhāva* takes the suffixes *-gha*, *-ṇa*, and *-pu*; likewise, the vowels *i* and *u* [are used] after words such as *gaha*.
Furthermore, the suffix *apaccaya* may also occur, and words beginning with *tu* and ending in *mādi* may serve as numerals.

From this point forward, the fact that these words are preceded by prefixes (*upasagga*) and the inclusion of sentences for the three tenses should be understood according to the method already stated; therefore, we shall present only the appropriate examples of such sentences.

*Āsa* means "to sit. That which is to be sat upon is *āsanaṃ*; that which is fit for sitting is *āsanīyaṃ*. *Kamma* means "to serve. One who is to be served is *upāsītabbo*, namely the teacher (*guru*); thus, he is *upāsanīyo*. *Sī* means "to lie down.

With the substitution of *e* and *ayā*, that which is to be lain upon is *sayanaṃ*; that which is fit for lying down by you is *sayanīyaṃ*. *Atisī* means "to surpass. That which is to be surpassed is *atisayitabbo*;

a mat (*kaṭa*) that is to be surpassed by you is *atisayanīyo*. *Pada* means "to go. By the rule "after *pada* etc., [the suffix] *yuk* [is added] optionally," the suffix *yuk* is applied; the letter *k* is for the purpose of causing the *kānubandha* (the *ka*-suffix).
The syllable *u* is for the purpose of pronunciation; *dassaja* is the original form. That which arises is *uppajjana*, *uppajjitabba*, and *uppajjanīya*.

That which is to be practiced is the path (*magga*) that is to be practiced (*paṭipajjitabba*) and is to be entered upon (*paṭipajjanīya*). *Budh* means knowledge; that which is awakened to is the Dhamma that is to be awakened to (*bujjhitabba*) and is to be realized (*bujjhanīya*).
*Su* means hearing; that which is heard is the Dhamma that is to be heard (*sotabba*). In the presence of the suffix *ññi*, there is the insertion of *n*: "of *ta*, *tha*, *na*, and *ra*"...

When *ṇ* is substituted for *ṭa-ṭha-ṇa-la*, the vowel *o* is absent according to the rule "there is no *o* in the case of *kā-anubandha* [roots] and *nāgama* [suffixes]. It is to be heard; it is worthy of being heard.
*Kara* means "doing. 95. *Pararūpa* [Rule]:

When there is a consonant following the letter *ya*, the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) occurs for a verbal root ending in *m* or *n* before a consonant other than *y*. Thus: *karīyati* means "that which is to be done" (the Dhamma), "worship to be performed," or "wholesome action to be performed."
119. In place of *tum*, *tun*, and *tabbe*, or in the case of *tum* and so forth, *karassā* may optionally occur. [Example: *kātabbaṃ hitaṃ* (benefit is to be done).
171. *rā* becomes *ṇo*.
The suffix *ṇa* does not occur after a verbal root ending in *ra*. [Thus: *karaṇīyo*. *Bhara* means "to support":

that which is supported (*bharīyati*) is "to be supported" (*bharaṇīyo*). *Gaha* means "to seize. According to the rule "for roots beginning with *ru* etc., the following *ma* is optionally replaced by *va*," the final vowel becomes *va*.
The letter *m* is a *nubandha* (indicatory letter). By the rule "ṇa replaces a *niggahīta*," the *niggahīta* becomes *ṇa*; thus: "that which is gathered" (*saṃgayhati*).
*Saṅgaṇhitabbo* means "to be gathered" or "to be embraced"; it is derived by taking the root *gaṇh* (to take) with the suffix *ṇa* according to the rule beginning with *tathana-rā*.

*Rama* means "in play"; that which is played with or enjoyed is called *ramaṇīyo vihāro* (a delightful monastery). *Āpa* means "to reach. According to the rule *sakāpānaṃ kukakū ṇe*, there is a division of the grammatical connection (*yogavibhāga*) into *sakāpānaṃ kuka* and *kū*.

With the augment *ū* and the substitution of the nasal augment (*nāgama*) for *ṇe*, one reaches—that is, it is to be attained—thus *pāpuṇitabbo*. By the rule of *pararūpa* (substitution of the subsequent form), it becomes *pattabbo* (to be reached).
*pāpuṇanīyo*, *pāpanīyo*. 96.
The *niggahīta* of words ending in *m* or *n* that denote an action becomes *y* before a consonant. [Example: *vaggantaṃ*, *gamiyati*. Thus.
*Gantabbo*, *gamitabbaṃ*, *gamanīyaṃ*. [The root] *khan* = *khaṇa* in the sense of digging;

with the substitution of the nasal stop (*niggahīta*) for the guttural (*vagganta*), it becomes *khaññati*, thus *khantabbaṃ*, *āvāṭaṃ khanitabbaṃ*, *khananīyaṃ*. [The root] *hana* in the sense of harming; *haññati*, thus *hantabbaṃ*, *hanitabbaṃ*, *hananīyaṃ*.
[The root] *mana* in the sense of knowing; *maññati*, thus *mantabbo*, *manitabbo*. [This is according to the rule: "In some cases, after words such as *pada*..."
*yuka*: when the *ca*-group (the letter *c*) and so forth have been applied, it is to be considered as *maññitabba* (to be thought) and *maññanīya* (to be thought).

*Pūja* = *pūjāyaṃ*. By the rule “*curādito ṇī*,” the suffix *ṇi* is added; because of the heaviness (*gurutta*) of the syllable *ñu*, there is the substitution of *o* for *ū* by the rule “*yuvaṇṇānaṃ eo paccaye*,” resulting in *pūje*. That which is to be worshipped (*pūjetabbo*)—with the suffix *ū*, there is the substitution of *a* for *e*—is *pūjayitabbo* or *pūjanīyo* (worthy of worship), [referring to] the Blessed One.

In the sense of the agent (*kattari*): *yā* = in the sense of reaching (*pāpuṇane*). That which is led forth (*nīyati*) is the *niyyāniyo maggo* (the path leading out). Those who go (*gacchanti*) are the *gamanīyā bhogā* (enjoyments to be experienced). In the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*): *naha* = in the sense of purification (*soceyye*).

That by which one bathes is *nahānīya*, namely bath-powder (*cuṇṇa*). In the sense of "giving" (*dāna*), with the prefix *sam-* and the root *pad* meaning "to give," that to whom [something] is properly given is a "recipient," such as a brahmin (*sampadāniyo brāhmaṇo*).
28. The suffix *-ghyaṇ*.

In the case of verbal roots denoting the sense of action (bhāva-kamma), the suffix *ghyaṇ* frequently occurs after a root ending in a consonant. When the vowel *ū* follows, the form becomes *kāriya*. From the root *hara* (in the sense of taking): that which is to be taken (*harīyati*) is *hāriya*.
From the root *bhara* (in the sense of bearing): that which is to be borne (*bharitabba*) is *bhāriya*. From the root *labha* (in the sense of obtaining):

according to the rule "after [consonants of] the *vagga*, *la*, and *sa*, there is *te*," the preceding vowel is substituted; then, by applying the rule "the fourth and second [consonants]" to the third vowel (*a*), that which is to be obtained (*labhitabba*) is *labbha*.
*Vaca* means "in speech.
98. *Kagā ca jānaṃ ghānubandhe*:
When followed by a nasal consonant (*gha*), the letters *ka* and *ga* [are substituted] for verbal roots ending in *ca* and *ja*, respectively, in accordance with their order.

84. When a suffix having *ṇ* as its indicatory letter (*ṇānubandha*) follows, the vowel *a* at the end [of the base] becomes *ā*. *Vacanaṃ vuccateti vākyaṃ*: "That which is spoken is called speech (*vākya*). *Bhaja*=in the sense of service;

that which is to be served is *bhāgya*, [the form] whose *g* has been elided. *Ci*=in the sense of accumulation; the act of accumulating, or that which is accumulated, is *ceyya*, [the form] whose doubling of consonants (*dvitta*) has occurred.
5,122. Regarding *nito c’ assa* and *parassa c’ assa*:

the *cha* (c) of the particle *ca* becomes *cho*. It is that which decides, thus it is "to be decided" (*viniccheyya*); in the case of the *nāgama*, it is "that which is to be decided" (*vinicchinitabba*).
In the substitution of *e* and *ayādesa*, [the forms] are *vinicchetabba* and *vinicchanīya*. The root *nī* means "to lead"; that which is led is "leadable" (*neyyo*).
*Neyya* means that which is to be led;

it is that which is to be guided. 29. After verbal roots ending in long *ā*, the suffix *ghyaṇ* occurs in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*) or the object (*karman*), and the final *ā* is changed to *e*. From the root *dā* (to give): *dātabbaṃ* = *deyyaṃ* (that which is to be given).
*Pā* means drinking; that which is drunk is *peyya*. *Mā* means measuring; that which is measured is *meyya*. *Ñā* means understanding; that which is known is *ñeyya*, meaning "to be known.

In the presence of the suffix *ū*, there is the augment *n*: according to the rule “*ñāssa ne + jā*,” the substitution of *jā* for *ñā* occurs, thus it is to be understood as *jānitabba*, i.e., *vijāniya*.
*Khā* means reckoning; that which is to be reckoned is *saṃkheyya*.

30. That which [ends in] *vada* and so forth, when used in the sense of verbal action (*kriyāttha*), commonly occurs in the senses of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*kamma*). *Vada* = speaking; that which goes toward speech is *vajja*. *Mada* = intoxication;
that by which one becomes intoxicated through the act of intoxicating is *majja*. *Gamanaṃ* (going) or *gammati* (is gone to) is *gammaṃ*.
In *gada* (to speak), that which is to be spoken is *gajja*; it sounds forth, thus it is *gajja*. In *pada* (to go), that which is to be gone upon is *pajja*, namely a verse (*gāthā*).
In *ada*/*khāda* (to eat), that which is eaten is *khajja*, namely food (*khādanīya*). In *dama* (to tame), that which is to be tamed is *damma*, namely one who is to be subdued.
By the rule of the *bhujā-nneti* group, the suffix *ya* is applied where *anna* (food) is to be expressed.
83. *Lahussūpantassati*:
For a light (*lahu*) vowel followed by a semivowel (*upanta*), the vowels *e* and *o* occur respectively. For example: *yassa pubbarūpe bhuñjitabbo* becomes *bhojjo odano*;
*bhojjā yāgu*. 31. *Kicca ghacca bhacca bhabba leyya*.

These words ending in the suffix *ya* are derived through *nipātana* (irregular formation). *Kara* means "doing" (*karaṇe*). By this *nipātana*, when the substitution of *kicca* is made, there is a prior form (*pubbarūpa*):

that which is to be done is "kicca. *Hana* means "to kill" (*hiṃsāyaṃ*). When the substitution of *ghacca* and so forth is made, it is "ghacca," meaning either "the act of killing" (*hananaṃ*) or "that which is killed" (*haññati*).

*Bhara* means "supporting" (*bharaṇe*). When the substitution of *bhacca* and so forth is made, that which is to be supported is "bhacca. *Bhū* means "existence" (*sattāyaṃ*). In the case of *yamhi*...

In the case of *okāra*, because it becomes [the suffix] *-bba* through this substitution (*avādesa*), it is called *bhabba*. In *liha* (meaning "to taste"), when there is the letter *ya* substituted for *ha* by this [rule], it becomes *lehitabba* or *leyya*;
here, there is the vowel-increment (*vuddhi*) of *ekāra*. 32. [The suffix] *yaka* is applied after roots such as *guha*.
The suffix *yaka* occurs after roots such as *guh* and others that denote an action, in the senses of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*kamma*).
*Guh* = to conceal. By the rule “*lahussupantassā*,” the final *o* is substituted for the *a* of the root; however, by the rule “*na te kānubandhanāgamesū*,” this substitution is prohibited.

Then, by the rule “*hassa vipallāso*,” there is a substitution (*vipallāsa*) of *h*. Thus, the act of concealing (*guhana*), that which is to be concealed (*guhitabba*), or what is concealed (*guyha*) is formed. *Duh* = to fill. The act of milking (*dohana*), or that which is milked (*duyhati*), is called *duyha*. *Sās* = instruction.
117. The form *sissa* or *sisso* occurs before a suffix beginning with *kā*. The preceding form [is applied]; thus, one who is taught (*sissīyati*) is a *sisso* (pupil).

These suffixes beginning with *tabba* are indeed established even when times such as the future (*pesā*), the present (*ti*), or the attainment of the highest goal (*sagga*) are implied, because they are prescribed by way of their general application.
*Pesana* (sending) is the commanding and requesting that "this must be done by you.

*Atisagga* (authorization) is the granting of permission for what is to be done—by way of demonstrating the proper practice—to one who has been asked, "What is this that I must do? such as, "Living beings must not be killed," and so forth.
*Pattakāla* (the right time) is the arrived occasion. One who acts after having examined the proper time for performing the duty [acts at the right time].
In that case, there is an announcement of the occasion (*samayārocana*), but no formal request (*ajjhesanā*) is present there. [Expressions such as] "The task must indeed be done by you, sir;
it is to be performed, it is to be executed, it is to be carried out, it is to be accomplished"—thus, "the task is to be done by you," for the time has arrived for you to perform the task.
In this way, they are established even when occurring in the future tense (*uddhamuhutta*) with respect to the agent (*pesādi*). Likewise, [they apply] to an agent who is capable and distinguished.
And when [the verb] is being understood as distinguished by the necessity of an obligation (*āvassaka-dhammīṇatā*), it is established from the perspective of its state (*bhāvādo*).
"The task must be performed by you after a moment. "The kingdom must be ruled by you; you are worthy. "The burden must be carried by you; you are capable.
"The task must necessarily be performed by you. "A debt must be paid by you."
33. *Kattari ltuṇkā*:

In the sense of the agent (*kattari kārake*), the suffixes *l* and *tuṇ* occur after verbal roots. In *kara*, for the purpose of the action (*karaṇe*), by the rule of single-substitution (*pararūpe*) and by the rule “*ltuṇpitādīnaṃ mā simhī*,” there is the elision of the vowel *ā*.
Thus: he does (*karoti*) = doer (*kattā*). Likewise: he supports (*bharati*) = supporter (*bhattā*). He carries (*harati*) = carrier (*hattā*). He splits (*bhidati*) = splitter (*bhettā*).
The letter *e* is split within the letter *ū*. One who cuts is a cutter (*chettā*). One who gives food is a giver of food (*bhojanadātā*).

One who joins together is a joiner (*sandhātā*). One who speaks is a speaker (*vattā*). Through the substitution of the following form for the letter *o*, one who eats is an eater (*bhottā*). By the rule “there is the insertion of *y* after words beginning with *pada* in certain cases,” there is the addition of *y*;

thus, one who awakens is an awakener (*bujjhitā*). One who knows is a knower (*ñātā*). One who cuts is a cutter (*chetā*). One who hears is a hearer (*sotā*). [This occurs] by the rule “*ū* + *lassa*.”

One who grasps the letter *ū* as *e* is a "grasper" (*gahetā*). One who comes into being is a "becomer" (*bhavitā*). One who remembers is a "rememberer" (*saritā*). Regarding the rule "the *niggahīta* [anusvāra] of the nasals":

because it goes to the *niggahīta* and to the end of the consonant groups, one who goes is a "goer" (*gantā*). The *niggahīta* also follows roots ending in *n*: one who digs is a "digger" (*khantā*); one who is pacified is a "pacifier" (*santā*);
one who conceives is a "conceiver" (*mantā*). One who protects is a "protector" (*pālayitā* or *pāletā*); here, the suffix *ṇi* is applied because the root belongs to the *curādi* class.

In the case of the suffixes *ṇi* and *ṇāpi*, [the forms] "one who causes to cultivate" (*bhāvayati*) are *bhāvayitā* and *bhāvetā*. Likewise: *sārayitā* and *sāretā*; *dāpayitā* and *dāpetā*; *hāpayitā* and *hāpetā*;
*nirodhayitā* and *nirodhetā*; *bodhayitā* and *bodhetā*; *ñāpayitā* and *ñāpetā*; *sāvayitā* and *sāvetā*;
*gāhayitā* and *gāhetā*; *kārayitā* and *kāretā*; *kārāpayitā* and *kārāpetā*, and so forth.

In the suffix *ṇa*, the letter *ṇ* serves the purpose of causing vowel strengthening (*vuddhi*). One who makes a chariot is a *rathakāraka*; here, by the rule “*assā ṇānubandhe*,” the *ā* is substituted [for the final vowel], and there is a compound ending in *ām*.
One who gives food is an *annadāyaka*. By the rule “*adhātussa kā+syādito ghe+ssī*,” when *gha* follows, *i* is the substitute for this [suffix];
thus, *annadāyikā* (a female giver of food) and *annadāyakaṃ kulaṃ* (a family that gives food). By the rule “*āssā+ṇāpimhi yuka*,” [the suffix] *ṇāpi* [is added] except in other cases.

*yuka*. One who leads the world is a *lokanāyaka*; in the case of the vowel *e*, there is the substitution of *āy* according to the rule "āy + vā ṇānubandhe. Likewise, one who guides is a *vināyaka*. With no object-word (*akamma-upapada*) preceding, one who performs is a *kāraka*;
similarly, a *dāyaka* (giver) and a *nāyaka* (leader). In the case of the vowel *o*, with the substitution of *āv*, one who hears is a *sāvaka* (disciple);
as before, with the vowel *i*, it becomes *sāvikā*. One who reaps is a *lāvaka*. *Pu* means purification; one who purifies is a *pāvaka* (fire). One who exists is a *bhāvaka* (cultivator).
One who waits upon (*upāsatī*) is an *upāsaka*. One who takes (*gaṇhāti*) is a *gāhaka*, a *pāvaka*, or a *yājaka*.

The root *vadha* means injury; one who injures (*vadheti*) is a *vadhaka*. In the phrase "also elsewhere," there is a prohibition of the vowel lengthening (*vuddhi*). By the rule "for *hana*, *ghāta* [is substituted] when a suffix beginning with *ṇ* follows," there is the substitution of *ghāta*; thus, one who kills (*hanati*) is a *ghātaka*. By the rule "for *maṃ* [the substitute *mum* is applied] after roots such as *rudh*," there is *maṃ*;
thus, one who obstructs (*rundhati*) is a *rundhaka*. Due to the weight of the syllable, there is no lengthening. Likewise, one who eats (*bhuñjati*) is a *bhuñjaka*.
One who buys wealth is a *kayaka* (buyer). One who protects is a *pālaka* (protector). One who honors is a *pūjaka* (worshipper). One who endures among those who eat is a *titikkhaka* (endurer).
One who investigates is a *vīmaṃsaka* (investigator), and so forth. One who drives away is a *panūdaka*; here the vowel is lengthened by the rule beginning with “*byañjane*” [Pāṇini 6.3.137].
In the expression “*bhītvā + naka*,” the form *ānaka* arises through the separation of the grammatical rule (*yogavibhāga*), and thus it is *ānaka*. As for *āssa*...
With the addition of the suffix *nakāra*, there is the substitution of *jā* for *ñā* according to the rule “*ñāssa ne jā*,” resulting in *jānanako*.

With the suffix *ṇāpi*: the root *aṇ* (from the *daṇḍaka* list) means “to command”; one who commands is an *āṇāpako*. Likewise, *saññāpako* (one who makes known) and *patiṭṭhāpako* (one who establishes). From *saṃ* + *pa* preceding *āpa* (meaning “to reach”), as in “one who causes one to reach Nibbāna” is a *nibbānasampāpako*. Examples include *kārāpako* (one who causes to do) and *kārāpikā* (female one who causes to do), and so forth.
